1.title: Alexander Questions FDA Nominee on Effects of the Administration's Hiring Freeze
1.description:
At today’s confirmation hearing for Dr. Scott Gottlieb to lead the Food and Drug Administration [FDA], Senate health committee chairman Lamar Alexander asked Dr. Gottlieb what he would do about the administration’s hiring freeze if confirmed. 

Alexander said, “When we were working on 21st Century Cures, I asked [former FDA commissioner Dr. Califf] his number one priority for the Food and Drug Administration. He said it was to be able to hire and pay personnel at the FDA so they could deal with these life-saving drugs and devices that are coming the way of the FDA. The administration has placed a hiring freeze that seems to be interfering with that. Should you be confirmed, what would you do about that?”

Gottlieb responded, “I understand how important a strong workforce is to FDA and helping FDA maintain its gold standard… I think it’s incumbent among us to have a world class workforce that we’re providing the proper tools to and the proper training to, to maintain that very high standard. I have, through my career and my time at the FDA, been committed to making sure we have a very strong workforce at FDA. I have spoken out about that, I will continue to make my views known on this issue.”

2.title: Alexander: Gottlieb Has Impressive Qualifications & Is the Right Person to Lead FDA
2.description:
In today’s Senate health committee hearing on the nomination of Dr. Scott Gottlieb to head the Food and Drug Administration, Chairman Lamar Alexander said Dr. Gottlieb has “impressive qualifications from nearly every perspective.”

He continued, “The Food and Drug Administration has always been important but there’s never been a more important time to capitalize on the significant funding Congress has given to medical research—and to realize the promise of 21st Century Cures. …The FDA affects nearly every single American and regulates about a quarter of all consumer spending in the United States—over $4 trillion annually… And my hope is that you will help move the agency forward – so that America’s patients benefit from the remarkable discoveries our nation’s researchers are working on.”

3.title: Alexander Ask Witnesses about Timeline for Reauthorizing User Fee Agreements
3.description:
Today, Senate health committee chairman Lamar Alexander questioned the witnesses at today’s hearing on the FDA user fee agreements on when Congress should finish its work to reauthorize these agreements. 

Alexander said, “You’ve done your job on time. Now it’s up to us to do our job on time…We have to finish by the end of July in order to avoid expiration of the agreements in October 1…We heard last week from FDA , but what would be the consequences from your point of view if Congress fails to act by the end of July to reauthorize these agreements?”

Scott Whitaker, president and CEO of the Advanced Medical Technology Association said, “I think I would associate myself with the remarks of Dr. Schuren. If he suggests that one-third of the workforce would be lost, that’s a huge hit to our industry. I think broadly it creates tremendous uncertainty for our industry. In many ways uncertainty is really the enemy of innovation. When you get hit with that uncertainty, it freezes company. We want to move as quickly as we can.”

4.title: Alexander: Timely FDA User Fee Reauthorization is “Integral to Helping Patients"
4.description: Today, Senate health committee chairman Lamar Alexander opened the second hearing on the reauthorization of the FDA user fee agreements, saying, “After reviewing the recommendations from industry and the FDA, I believe these are good agreements for patients. I look forward to working with Senator Murray and our other members to approve these agreements here in committee and move them to the floor in a timely manner, so patients and the agency and the industry have some certainty. …Patients were involved in developing the commitment letters, and we have already begun receiving support from patient groups asking us to reauthorize the agreements expeditiously.”

5.title: Alexander, Corker Introduce Bill to Rescue Americans with Zero Options for Insurance on the ACA
5.description:
Today, Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor about legislation he introduced with Sen. Bob Corker to rescue Americans with Affordable Care Act subsidies who have zero options for health insurance on the exchanges for the 2018 plan year.
Alexander said, “There are 34,000 Knoxville area residents who rely on an Affordable Care Act subsidy to purchase insurance, and after the one remaining insurer pulled out of the exchange for 2018, these subsidies are worth as much as bus tickets in a town with no buses running… This legislation would help those in Knoxville and across the country by allowing any American who receives a subsidy and has no insurance available on their exchange next year to use that subsidy to buy any state-approved insurance off of the exchange. Second, the bill would waive the Affordable Care Act requirement that these Americans, who have zero insurance options with their subsides, have to pay a penalty for not purchasing insurance.  And third, this legislation will help bring peace of mind between now and the beginning of next year to millions of Americans, some of the most vulnerable people in the country, who face having zero options of health insurance to purchase with their subsidy.”

6.title: Alexander and Labor Secretary Nominee Acosta Discuss Obama Administration’s 'Joint Employer' Rule
6.description:
Today, at the Senate labor committee hearing on Alexander Acosta’s nomination to serve as secretary of labor, Chairman Lamar Alexander said: “One area where American workers are still able to fit into the workplace is with our franchisees. I think the number is about 700,000 Americans who have franchises, in other words, they have an opportunity, typically in their hometown, to take restaurant franchises or some other franchise and typically they would work 12 hours a day for many years—often it’s a family working for many years—and it’s a way that you can still live in your home community and work in your home community and be reasonably independent and move your way into the middle class.”

Alexander then asked: “In order to be treated as the employer of an employee, shouldn’t the business-person have direct and immediate control over an employee?”

Acosta responded: “That is one of the traditional criteria, Senator.”

Alexander: “Do you believe that indirect control or even unexercised potential to control working conditions could make a franchisor and franchisee joint employers?”

Acosta: “That would be an untraditional approach.”

Alexander: “Do you think that the person, who hires, fires, pays, sets work hours, and issues directions to employees should be considered the employer?”

Acosta: “That is the usual approach, Senator.”

7.title: Alexander and Labor Sec. Nominee Acosta Discuss Skills Gap and Overtime Rule
7.description:
Today, at the Senate labor committee hearing on Alexander Acosta’s nomination to serve as secretary of labor, Chairman Lamar Alexander asked, “If we were to think of you, as I think we should, as ‘Secretary of the Workforce’ to help workers—in this head-spinning environment that we find ourselves in—adjust to it and fit in to it … if you see that, according to the Manufacturing Institute, 2 million Americans’ manufacturing jobs will go unfilled over the next 10 years due to the skills gap, specifically, what are some of the things we should be doing about it?”

Acosta responded, “I think it’s critical, if confirmed, that the Department of Labor work very closely with the Department of Education because there is a lot of spending that is taking place in education, and we want to make sure, to the extent possible and feasible, that individuals have the opportunity to align their education with the skills the workplace will demand. More specifically, to the second part of your question, you mentioned apprenticeships… I think if you look at some of the apprenticeship programs where individuals work and they get credit while they are working, or some of the other programs that are available at community colleges that focus on vocational opportunities in partnership with individual businesses, those are all options that we should be looking at, because they are alternative ways of educating. They are alternative ways of providing skills. And importantly, it is a way for students to acquire skills to be used in jobs without taking on the enormous debt that we’re seeing in some secondary programs right now.

8.title: Alexander: Goal of Labor Sec., Congress is to Create Environment for Workers to Succeed
8.description:
Today, Senate labor committee Chairman Lamar Alexander began the confirmation hearing for Secretary of Labor nominee Alexander Acosta by saying that the Labor Secretary and Congress’s goal is to create an environment for American workers to succeed in a rapidly changing workplace and that harmful Obama-era labor regulations have only made it harder for Americans to create, find, or keep good-paying jobs.
Alexander said, “The issue for workers today is not whether they belong to a union. It is whether they have the skills to adapt to the changing marketplace and to find and keep a job—to be accurate, to create and keep a job.  My generation found jobs.  This generation is more likely to have to create their own jobs.”

He continued, “Tom Friedman says that probably the most important governance challenge is a great need ‘to develop the learning systems, training systems, management systems, social safety nets, and government regulations that would enable citizens to get the most out of these accelerations and cushion their worst impacts.’ One of the federal government’s chief actors in this drama should be the Secretary of Labor.”

9.title: Alexander Questions FDA Witnesses on Effects of Delay of User Fee Reauthorization
9.description:
Today, Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander questioned FDA witnesses, including Dr. Janet Woodcock, Director for Drug Evaluation and Research at FDA, on the impact on patients if the FDA user fee agreements were not reauthorized on time. 

Alexander asked, “ “[I]f Congress does not act by the end of July, 60 days before the expiration of the current agreements, what would be the impact on the Food and Drug Administration if we fail to do that… An application for a cancer therapy or cure that might be beforereviewers, might be delayed?”

Dr. Woodcock said, “Yes, and we know right now that we have patients living hand to mouth, young people with brain tumors or other cancers that are waiting for the next effective therapy to come along as they develop resistance. I heard from an ex-staffer about this, who has lived a long time and been able to work because there have been successive approvals of drugs for his cancer that have kept him alive. This would be repeated over and over, and, most concerning I think, in the biologics area, for the pharmaceuticals, the gene therapies, the cellular therapies, the very innovative therapies require oversight and investigational phase, because any slip-up there can last for 10 years and set the entire field back.”

10.title: Alexander: Congress Owes Patients and Their Families a Prompt Reauthorization of FDA User Fees
10.description:
Today, Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander opened the first hearing on the reauthorization of the FDA’s user fee agreements, saying, “We ended last year passing the 21st Century Cures Act, which Leader McConnell called ‘the most important piece of legislation’ that year. 94 Senators voted for the legislation, which also had the support of President Obama and Vice President Biden. Today, we are here to talk about how we continue funding the FDA, the agency responsible for making sure the promising research supported by 21st Century Cures actually reaches patients.”
He stressed the importance of completing the reauthorization on time, saying, “The authority for FDA to collect user fees for medical product review will expire on September 30 of this year – six months from now.  
“If we do not move quickly to reauthorize these agreements, in late July, the FDA will be forced to begin sending layoff notices to more than 5,000 employees to notify them that they may lose their job in 60 days.  
 
“A delay in reauthorizing these agreements would delay the reviews of drugs and devices submitted after April 1. 
“For example, if we do not pass these reauthorizations into law before the current agreements expire, an FDA reviewer who gets started reviewing a cancer drug submitted to the agency in April would be laid off on October 1, before the reviewer is able to finish his or her work.
“The sooner we reauthorize the agreements, the better -- to give patients, reviewers, and companies certainty.”

11.title: Alexander: Obama-era Ed. Reg. is in “Direct Violation of Law that 85 Sens. Voted for 15 Months Ago”
11.description:
In a speech today on the Senate floor, Senate education Chairman Lamar Alexander said that the Senate is poised to overturn an Obama administration education regulation that "is in direct violation of the law that 85 senators voted for just 15 months ago." 

Alexander said, “In 2015, 85 United States senators voted for the law fixing No Child Left Behind that reversed the trend to a National School Board and restored decisions to classroom teachers, local school boards, and states. The Wall Street Journal said it was ‘the largest devolution of federal control to the states in a quarter-century.’ The Department of Education regulation that this resolution seeks to overturn does exactly the reverse – it begins to restore the National School Board and takes away responsibility from classroom teachers and local school boards. It does this in direct violation of the law that 85 senators voted for just 15 months ago.

“So the question before us today is not only whether we believe in a National School Board or we believe in local school boards. But more important perhaps is the question of who writes the law: Does Congress write the law, or does the Department of Education?”

12.title: Alexander Questions Witness on Status of Universal Flu Vaccine
12.description:
This morning at a hearing of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies, Sen. Alexander talked with Dr. Stacey Schultz-Cherry with the Department of Infectious Diseases at St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital in Memphis, about the status of a universal flu vaccine. 

Sen. Alexander, who also chairs the Senate health committee, asked, “[The] flu is a real problem. You have a center which monitors that and keeps after that at St. Jude’s. Tell us about what you did with the H1N1 pandemic in 2009, the effect of the center and keeping up with that and with subsequent outbreaks and what your estimate is about whether we’re likely to have a vaccine for universal flu.”     

Dr. Schultz-Cherry responded, “…Is a universal flu vaccine in the works? Absolutely. And is it something that we can accomplish? Yes, I think it is. I think it’s realistic to think that we will have a vaccine that will provide some protection against the strains of influenza that we’ve currently identified as well as those that we haven’t...”

Alexander responded, “Do you agree with [Director of the National Institutes of Health] Dr. Collins that could occur in the next decade?”

Cherry replied, “Yes, I actually do. I think we’re making great strides and there [are] many people focused on creating a universal flu vaccine. I think it is something that can be accomplished.”

13.title: Alexander: New Education Secretary Will Restore Tennessee Classrooms to Tennessee Communities
13.description:
Today, Senate education Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor ahead of the confirmation vote for Betsy DeVos to serve as Secretary of Education. 
He said, "I'm voting for Betsy DeVos because she will implement our law fixing No Child Left Behind the way we wrote it, to restore control to classroom teachers and legislators. And because she has been at the forefront of public charter schools and worked tirelessly to give low-income children more of the same kind of choices wealthy families have.  Betsy DeVos has committed to … no more national school board, no Washington mandates for vouchers, no Washington mandates for Common Core, no Washington mandates for specific kinds of teacher evaluation.”

14.title: Alexander Questions Witnesses at Hearing on the Obamacare Emergency in Individual Insurance Market
14.description:
Today, at a Senate health committee hearing, Chairman Lamar Alexander questioned Tennessee Insurance Commissioner Julie Mix McPeak, President and CEO of America's Health Plans Marilyn Tavenner, and CEO of the National Association of Health Underwriters Janet Trautwein on stabilizing the individual health insurance market and the timing of doing so. 

Alexander asked, "Is it possible to work just on the individual market …and leave for a separate discussion what we do about Medicaid and what we do about the employer market?”

In response, Commissioner McPeak said, "Absolutely yes, I believe you can address the individual market separately from the other categories of care, and that’s where the real need is and the timing is critical. … I think that you need to provide some indication to plans as quickly as possible, but March I think would be extremely helpful."

15.title: Alexander Chairs Hearing on the Obamacare Emergency in Individual Insurance Market
15.description:
Today, Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander chaired a hearing on ways to address the Obamacare emergency in the individual health insurance market. 
Alexander said, "“In my home state of Tennessee, in September of 2016, we woke up one morning and Blue Cross Blue Shield announced that it was pulling out of Nashville, Memphis, and Knoxville.  That’s 131,000 people who had Blue Cross insurance in the individual market.  And they wouldn’t be able to buy it in 2017.  So they don’t have that option this year.”
He continued, “That’s an alarm bell in every one of those homes. It’s a lot of trouble when you lose your insurance option. And in two-thirds of our counties in Tennessee, people who buy their insurance through the exchanges only have one option now.  And that’s true in a third of the counties across the country.”
“We may reach a situation in 2018 where many Americans have a subsidy through the Affordable Care Act to buy insurance in the individual market, but they don’t have any insurance to buy.  It’d be like having a bus ticket in a town where no buses run. Right now in two thirds of our counties we’ve got only one bus running through town and in 2018 we might have zero. That’s the problem to solve.”

16.title: Alexander: Betsy DeVos Nomination Heads to Senate Floor
16.description:
Today, the Senate education committee favorably reported out the nomination of Betsy DeVos to become the next Secretary of Education.  

Chairman Alexander said, “Betsy DeVos is on our children’s side. On charter schools and school choice, she is in the mainstream of those trying to help children succeed and her critics are outside of it. I am proud that our education committee has favorably reported out her nomination, and I urge my colleagues to support her confirmation when it comes to a vote on the Senate floor.”

Read more HERE: http://bit.ly/2jREFtK

17.title: Alexander: Betsy DeVos has spent 30 years trying to help low-income children attend a better school
17.description:
Today, Senate education Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor in support of President Trump's nominee for Secretary of Education. 

Alexander said, "Next Tuesday, we will vote on whether to approve Betsy DeVos's nomination to the office of United States Education Secretary and will send that to the floor of the full Senate. I'm confident that we will do that. I'm confident the Senate will approve her. Even though they may disagree with her, Democrats should give the new president a chance to have his own Education Secretary just as we did -- just as Republicans did for President Obama. Few Americans have done as much as Betsy DeVos has to help low-income children have a choice of a better school. The Democrats' opposition to her says more about them than it does about her."

18.title: Alexander Questions Price on His Goals of Obamacare Repeal & Replacement
18.description: During questions to Dr. Price, Alexander said, “My belief is the historic mistake in passage of Affordable Care Act was that it sought to expand a [health care] system that already costs too much.” Alexander then asked Dr. Price about repairing the damage of Obamacare and the goals of lowering the cost of insurance for Americans, giving them more choices of lower-cost insurance, and putting more decisions in the hands of states and into the hands of patients.

19.title: Alexander to Price: We Will Work to Rescue Americans Trapped in Collapsing Obamacare System
19.description:
Today, at the Senate health committee  hearing on the nomination of Rep. Tom Price (R-Ga.) to lead the Department of Health and Human Services, Chairman Alexander that Obamacare should be repealed and replaced simultaneously and concurrently as President-elect Trump and Speaker Paul Ryan have also suggested.

He continued, "To me, ‘simultaneously’ and ‘concurrently’ means Obamacare should be finally repealed only when there are concrete, practical reforms in place that give Americans access to truly affordable health care. The American people deserve health care reform that’s done in the right way, for the right reasons, in the right amount of time. It’s not about developing a quick fix. It’s about working toward long-term solutions that work for everyone.”

20.title: Alexander: Ed. Sec. Nominee Betsy DeVos is On Our Children's Side
20.description:
Caption: At today’s hearing on the nomination of Betsy DeVos to lead the U.S. Department of Education, education committee Chairman Lamar Alexander said, “ Betsy DeVos is on our children’s side. On charter schools and school choice, she is in the mainstream of those trying to help children succeed and her critics are outside of it…
He continued saying, “We are fortunate that Betsy DeVos is President-elect’s Trump nominee for U.S. Education Secretary, I am going to do my best to support her confirmation and look forward to working with her.”

21.title: Alexander Speaks on Senate Floor Ahead of Cures Cloture Vote
21.description:
Ahead of today’s vote to move forward on 21st Century Cures, Senate health committee chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor about the bipartisan support for this legislation that holds the promise of improving the life and health of virtually every family in the country. 
He said, “Mr. President, the United States Senate Majority Leader…has said more than once…that the 21st Century Cures bill on which we will be voting in a few minutes is the most important legislation Congress will pass in year. 

“In his address to the nation this past weekend, President Obama urged us to vote for the bill today and tomorrow. ‘It could help us find a cure for Alzheimer's,’ the president said. ‘It could end cancer as we know it and help those seeking treatment for opioid addiction.’ The president continued, ‘It is an opportunity to save lives and an opportunity we must can't miss.’

“Vice President Biden has been telephoning senators, urging support for 21st Century Cures because, in the vice president's words, ‘it is a big step’ for cancer research and the cancer moonshot that's so close to his heart.

“Speaker Paul Ryan in the House of Representatives has made 21st Century Cures explicitly a centerpiece of his vision for our country's future, describing it as ‘bipartisan legislation that would accelerate the discovery, development, and delivery of lifesaving treatments.’ With such bipartisan support from the President of the United States, the Vice President of the United States, the Speaker of the House, the Senate Majority Leader, two Democrats, two Republicans, it's no wonder that last Wednesday the House of Representatives approved 21st Century Cures by the overwhelming vote of 392-26.”

22.title: Alexander Speaks On Senate Floor on Bipartisan Support of Cures
22.description:
Today, Chairman Alexander spoke on the Senate floor ahead of  House's vote tonight on 21st Century Cures. 

He said, "This is legislation that has the strong support of the President of the United States [and] the active support of the Vice President of the United States. Speaker Ryan in the House has said that it is important part of his agenda for health care for the future, and the Majority Leader, Senator McConnell, has said he believes it's the most important piece of legislation Congress could enact this year."

23.title: Alexander Speaks on Senate Floor Ahead of Cures Vote in House
23.description:
Chairman Alexander spoke on the floor today in advance of a vote tomorrow in the House on the 21st Century Cures bill. 

Alexander said he expects “a big vote over there.” And added, “I expect a big vote over here. I don't think there are senators who want to vote against opioid funding in their states. I don't think there will be a lot of senators who want to vote ‘no’ on more money to fight cancer and to help the vice president with the Cancer Moonshot. I suspect there will be a lot of senators who will want to vote ‘yes’ to help the president advance his precision medicine legacy.”

He said, “It's a really remarkable two years of work. it's involved many, many, many hearings, dozens of meetings, and this has been done in a large committee of 22 senators of very different points of view in a largely bipartisan way.”

24.title: Alexander: Bipartisan Advancing Hope Act Helps Deliver Treatments to Children With Rare Diseases
24.description:
Today, Senate health committee Chairman Alexander spoke on the Senate floor on the bipartisan Advancing Hope Act – which continues for five years a successful program driving faster treatments and cures to children with rare diseases. 

After Senate Democrats objected to Senator Casey’s (D-Pa.) attempt to pass the bipartisan legislation by unanimous consent, Alexander said: “Here's what the doctors at Saint Jude's hospital say about the proposal that Senator Isakson and Senator Casey have made that's been in the law since 2012 and that received 20 votes in our committee against the two votes of the senators who are on the floor: They said—this is a St. Jude doctors who have taken care of these very sick children—‘Priority Review Vouchers provide a powerful incentive to stimulate drug development in rare pediatric diseases.’ These aren't some people in Washington in bureaucracies. These are doctors caring for dying children. ‘These conditions,’ say the doctors, ‘often lack the market opportunity to attract significant investments or may present other significant development obstacles and costs that may deter investment for biopharmaceutical companies … [W]e've witnessed strong evidence … that the programs are working.’ The Isakson-Casey bill is working. ‘Support for the voucher program is key to facilitating access to new agents important to improving outcomes in pediatric cancers.’”

25.title: Alexander: FDA Proposed "Double Regulation" Could Halt Tests Americans Depend on For Treatment
25.description:
Today U.S. Sen. Lamar Alexander said that under the FDA’s proposal to regulate laboratory-developed tests, which Alexander pointed out are already regulated by an arm of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS), “the biggest loser, it seems to me, would be Americans who stand to benefit from the rapid pace of science and discovery.”

At a hearing of the Senate health committee, which Alexander chairs, he said that this amounts to unnecessary “double regulation” and offered an example of what this added burden could mean for medical innovation and patients who benefit from it. 

Vanderbilt University Medical Center performs 105 lab-developed tests, which Alexander said are “medical tests designed, manufactured and used in a single laboratory.” If just one of these 105 tests were subject to FDA approval, it could cost Vanderbilt $30-75 million to go through the process. And the possibility that any or all of the remaining 104 could be subject to the lengthy, costly FDA approval process could make costs prohibitive. “You can quickly see how costs could add up—even into the billions,” Alexander said. 
 
Alexander continued: “The Chair of the Department of Laboratory Medicine at the University of Washington wrote Sen. Murray and me suggesting the proper approach would be to modernize the [current] system to ‘promote continued patient access to affordable, high-quality tests without duplicative regulations.’”

26.title: Alexander Announces Bill Allowing States to Offer Americans More Health Insurance Options for 2017
26.description:
This morning on the Senate floor, Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander announced legislation that would give states the authority to allow those Americans who rely on Obamacare subsidies to have more options to buy insurance and would exempt the state from the individual mandate for the 2017 plan year. 

He said, “This bill addresses an emergency. … Here’s an example: If you’re a single mother in Memphis who gets an Obamacare subsidy to buy health insurance for your family, you might have read that Tennessee’s insurance commissioner says your rates may be more than 60 percent higher for the same health insurance policy next year.”

Alexander described the legislation saying, “Number one, it gives states with a failing Obamacare exchange the authority to allow residents to use their Obamacare subsidy to purchase any health care plan of their choice, even those off the exchange for the 2017 plan year… “It will give governors the opportunity to step in if he or she determines this emergency relief is ‘necessary to ensure that residents of the state have access to an adequate number of affordable private health insurance options in the individual or small group markets.’

“So this bill means the mother in Memphis can shop around for a health insurance policy that meets her family's needs but is unavailable on the exchange in Tennessee. And now when she goes to pay for it, she can use the Obamacare subsidy currently limited to exchange plans… 

“The second thing this bill does is this: If the state chooses to use this authority to allow residents to use subsidies outside of the exchange, the legislation will waive the Obamacare law's requirement that you must buy a specific health plan or pay a fine of as much as $2,000 for a family of four next year. In other words, if that mother can't find affordable insurance options that meet her family's needs, meaning a plan that covers the right doctors and services, on the Obamacare exchange, then she doesn't have to waste her money or the taxpayer's money on a plan that she doesn't want or doesn't need. And she won't be threatened with paying a fine if she doesn't.”

27.title: Alexander: Republicans Didn't Create Problem of Obamacare, But We're Prepared to Solve It
27.description:
Today, Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor about the alarming number of health insurance companies leaving Obamacare exchanges and the need to act on behalf of Americans struggling with the cost of health insurance. Alexander said he intends to introduce legislation soon to “provide relief” from “the cost of health insurance and a lack of options on the Obamacare exchanges.” 

Alexander said, “Unfortunately, I don't need to look any further than my home state of Tennessee to see how bad things have become. When Tennesseans woke up on August 24 and read the front page of our state's largest newspaper, they saw this headline: ‘Very near collapse.’ …What does very near collapse mean in the real world? This November, when Tennesseans are signing up for 2017 Obamacare plans, there will be fewer plans to choose from, and they'll be much more expensive. And this picture will be the same across the country.” 

He continued, “Next year, Tennesseans will be paying intolerable increases. On average between 44% and 62% more for their Obamacare plans than they paid last year … And if you, the policyholder, don't pay all of that, then you, the taxpayer, will. Because a large portion of Obamacare premiums are subsidized with tax dollars. Surely it's no valid excuse to say that just because taxpayers are paying most of the bill that justifies having a failing insurance market where costs are so out of control that we may soon have a situation where no insurance company is willing to sell insurance on an Obamacare exchange.”

“Millions of Americans need relief from Obamacare,” Alexander said. “Here's the action that's needed: First, Americans need immediate relief from the cost of health insurance and a lack of options on the Obamacare exchanges. We should do that by giving states more flexibility to give individuals and their families options to purchase lower-cost, private health insurance plans outside of Obamacare and we should do that now. I intend to offer legislation that would provide that relief. That is only to deal with the emergency of next year, 2017. Second, we need a big, structural change in order to avoid a near collapse of our nation's health insurance market. If there's a Republican in the White House next year, we need to repeal Obamacare and replace it with step-by-step reforms that transform the health care delivery system, by putting patients in charge, giving them more choices and reducing the cost of health care so that more people can afford it. But if there is a Democrat in the White House, broad systemic structural changes will still be necessary. Republicans didn't create this problem, but we're prepared to solve it. ”

28.title: Alexander: Tennessee Insurance Commissioner Says State Obamacare Exchange Is “Very Near Collapse”
28.description:
Senate health Chairman Lamar Alexander highlighted The Tennessean’s Wednesday front-page headline, which read: “Very Near Collapse”—words used by Tennessee’s insurance commissioner to describe the state of Tennessee’s Obamacare insurance exchange. Alexander said this is “happening in states all over the country as Obamacare plans and rates get locked in for next year.”
Alexander said that “Americans have a choice this election. You know exactly what Democrats will do if they are in charge. Democrats will increase Washington’s control of your private health insurance choices. Democrats will spend more of your taxpayer dollars to prop up the collapsing Obamacare exchanges.”
Alexander contrasted this approach with what Republicans have proposed.
“We want to help Americans struggling with the cost of health insurance immediately. We would do that by giving states more flexibility to give individuals and their families options to purchase lower-cost private health insurance plans outside of Obamacare,” he said.

29.title: Alexander on FOX News: Tennessean’s Eyesight Recovery Underscores Need for Congress to Pass Cures
29.description: Today, Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander and Tennessean Doug Oliver, who regained his sight after participating in a clinical trial where his own stem cells were injected into his eyes, were interviewed by Shannon Bream on Fox News Sunday. Alexander talked about how passing 21st Century Cures would unleash biomedical innovation and help more Americans take advantage of remarkable medical advances like the treatment that helped Oliver. He said, “Dr. Francis Collins, head of the National Institutes of Health, says within the next ten years we'll be using stem cells from your own body to restore a diseased heart. Up to now you've got to have a heart transplant. He says we'll have a vaccine for Zika, a vaccine for HIV/AIDS. We'll be able to identify Alzheimer's before you see its symptoms.”

30.title: Alexander Questions State & Local Ed. Administrators on Timeline of Proposed ESSA Regulation
30.description:
At this morning’s third oversight hearing on the new law fixing No Child Left Behind, Chairman Alexander talks with witnesses Dr. Stephen Pruitt, Kentucky Commissioner of Education, Dr. Gail Pletnick, an Arizona superintendent, and Dr. Linda Darling-Hammond, President and CEO at Learning Policy Institute and Professor of Education at Stanford University about a timeline for creating accountability systems and state academic standards. 

He asked Dr. Pruitt, “Would it make sense to you that Kentucky could develop its new accountability system during the next school year and then begin to identify new schools in the following year, which would be 18/19?

Dr. Pruitt said, “…what giving us that extra time would do would give us more time to really engage our stakeholders to ensure that we actually have buy in on the system. For me, a big part of this new accountability system has to be built on more trust between the state and local levels.”

Alexander later said, “It is my hope that Secretary King will announce before long that it would be appropriate under the new law because it was my intention at least that states would create their own accountability systems in the school year coming up, keep working with the already identified schools, but then begin to implement the new systems in the following year. … Dr. Pletnick, in about five different places in the law we try to make clear that the U.S. Department of Education cannot tell Arizona what its academic standards should be. We changed the word from ‘demonstrate’ to ‘assure’.  We put specific prohibitions in the law. …Do you believe that the U.S. Secretary of Education could decide to reject Arizona’s academic standards if he chose to?”

Dr. Pletnick said, “I believe that that is the way that I would interpret it and my fear is that others would as well, so this debate could start again over Common Core when we’re just starting to move forward and we really look at our standards and improve them.”

Alexander replied, “Do you read anything in the law to suggest that the U.S. Department of Education should be able to tell Arizona what its standards should be?”

Pletnick said, “I did not, and, as Arizona, we did not. We started the work on reviewing and revising standards so that they would better reflect what our state’s needs were.”

31.title: Alexander: The 4 Areas of Proposed Accountability Regulation Most in Need of Overhaul
31.description:
At this morning’s fifth oversight hearing on the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA), Chairman Alexander outlined the four areas in need of overhaul in the Dept. of Ed's proposed accountability rule on the new law fixing No Child Left Behind. 

Alexander said, “I am focused on four areas of the regulation that seem to the most in need of overhaul: the timeline for new state accountability systems, the summative rating system, the requirement for evidence of state academic standards, and the return to high stakes federal tests.”

32.title: Alexander: Democrats Wrong to Stand in Way of Opioids, Zika Legislation
32.description:
Today, Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor urging Senate Democrats to drop opposition to legislation that would address the opioids and Zika crises. 

On addressing the opioid abuse epidemic, Alexander said, “So, what's the problem? Well, our friends on the other side say, ‘You need to fund it.’ We are funding it. And they [Democrats] helped fund it. We've increased funding for opioids already by 542 percent. For those working on their math, that's five times more than we were doing two and a half years ago.”

33.title: Alexander Questions Sec. King On Ed Dept.’s Proposed Timeline for Accountability Regulations
33.description:
At this morning’s fourth oversight hearing on the new law fixing No Child Left Behind, Chairman Alexander questioned Secretary King about the department’s proposed timeline for implementing accountability regulations. 
Alexander said, “"When we wrote the law, we envisioned the states would have time to plan for the transition of the law. You’ve heard and we’ve heard some states say that your proposed regulation account doesn’t permit a state to do this. Now, let me ask you if what I’m about to describe would be an appropriate timeline for a state in your view: that states would develop and implement their new accountability systems during the school year that begins in 2017 and 2018, that’s next year. That means they’d be collecting data in that year. Then, in the following year: 2018/19, they would be identifying new schools in need of improvement. That would leave the year coming up, 2016/17, as a transition year during which I would assume states would continue to work with their already identified schools, although some states might want to move more rapidly. Would your proposed regulation allow that sort of schedule?”

34.title: Alexander: Congress Chose Words Carefully When We Wrote the Law Fixing No Child Left Behind
34.description: At this morning’s fourth oversight hearing on the new law fixing No Child Left Behind, Chairman Alexander told Education Secretary John King that the words Congress used to write the law  "were debated and carefully and deliberately chosen. We meant for the words to mean what they say – nothing more, nothing less."

35.title: Alexander: Admin. “Time Card Rule” Gives Control From Hands of Americans to Washington Bureaucrats
35.description:
Today, Senate labor committee Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor about the resolution he introduced with Senator Ron Johnson (R-Wisc.) to block implementation of the administration’s “Time Card Rule,” also known as the Overtime Rule, which Alexander said “could raise tuition by hundreds of dollars for millions of American college students or cause layoffs at universities” and leave workers punching the clock when they come and go from work and unable to negotiate a flexible work arrangement. 

Alexander said, “The administration calls this the overtime rule. I think we should call this the time card rule or the higher tuition rule. This means that a mid-level manager in Knoxville or Nashville who is making $40,000 a year is going to have to go back to punching a timecard. This affects 4.23 million workers nationwide, nearly 100,000 in Tennessee. It's going to create huge costs for employers including small businesses, nonprofits like the Boy Scouts, colleges and universities. They have to decide whether to cut services, cut benefits, lay off, demote employees or create more part-time job… This rule says the Obama administration knows best. They know how to manage your career, your work schedule, your free time, your income. They know better than you do.”

36.title: Alexander Talks On Senate Floor About Medical Breakthroughs Cures Could Bring
36.description:
Today, Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor about the Senate health committee's work on its companion to the House-passed 21st Century Cures legislation. Alexander said, “If the Senate finishes its work and passes these bipartisan biomedical innovation bills as well as a surge of funding for the National Institutes of Health and takes advantage of these advancements in science, we can help more patients live longer and healthier lives, and help more researchers who want to look the parent of a child in the eye and say we found a cure.”

He said there was “no excuse for [the Senate] not to get a result this year. And it would be extraordinarily disappointing to millions of Americans if we did not. 

Alexander shared recent examples of the attention on this exciting time in biomedical innovation, including a New York Times Magazine special health issue in advancements in cancer research, a pediatric cancer fundraising campaign by "Humans of New York" photographer Brandon Stanton—as well as a Wall Street Journal op-ed by doctors and former senators Bill Frist and Tom Coburn on the Senate's work to help bring safe treatments and cures to doctors' offices and patients’ medicine cabinets more quickly.

37.title: Alexander: DOL Fiduciary Rule Would Cost Middle-Class As Much  As $80B in Lost Retirement Savings
37.description:
Today, Senate labor Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor against the Labor Department’s fiduciary rule, which will restrict access to basic retirement planning advice for all but the wealthiest Americans.
Alexander said the fiduciary rule “will force ordinary Americans to go it alone, to try to make the best guess they can about how to manage their money for retirement. ...Americans with smaller retirement savings or Americans who are just getting started out saving for retirement are at the greatest risk for losing access to affordable retirement advice."

He added, “Let's look at what happened when a similar rule was implemented in the United Kingdom. The result was that people with smaller savings accounts lost access to retirement advice. Many firms quit providing face-to-face advice for small accounts. A quarter of all small firms were forced to close shop all together. The United Kingdom's four largest banks have all raised the minimum assets levels for clients to receive advice: $80,000 American dollars at one bank, $160,000 at another, $355,000 at a third, $800,000 at a fourth due to the new rule. So to access retirement accounts at the United Kingdom's biggest banks, you have to have at least $80,000 in your account. So what would that look like here in the United States? 77% of 401(k) Balances in the United States are below $80,000. The lowest threshold. 99.2% of the 401(k) Balances in the United States are below the $800,000 threshold. So if United States banks respond like United Kingdom's banks did to this rule, we might find that less than 1% of Americans will be rich enough to receive retirement advice at one of our nation's largest banks. We should call this the only the rich retire rule.” 

Chairman Alexander has joined with Sens. Isakson and Enzi in introducing a Congressional Review Act resolution of disapproval to overturn the Labor Department’s rule.

38.title: Alexander Asks What Ed Dept.’s Proposed SNS Regulation Might Mean for Future Regulations
38.description:
At this morning’s third oversight hearing on the new law fixing No Child Left Behind, Chairman Alexander talks with witnesses Dr. Nora Gordon, Associate Professor at the McCourt School of Public Policy at Georgetown University, and American Federation of Teachers President Randi Weingarten about the education department's proposed “Supplement, not Supplant,” regulation. 
Alexander asks Weingarten “What about what the department doing with this proposed regulation worries you about what might happen with future regulations?”
Weingarten replied, “The fact that the department keeps doing same old, same old, in terms of trying to rewrite history in terms of ‘supplement not supplant’ as opposed to really thinking about how do we ensure that there is flexibility that looks at what kids need through the lense of the practitioners is what is concerning all of us [on] any number of issues… It is whittling away the good will that all of us have to actually help all kids succeed, particularly our most vulnerable kids.”

39.title: Alexander: Administration "Earned an 'F'" on First Opportunity To Write ESSA Regulations
39.description: At this morning’s third oversight hearing on the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA), the new law fixing No Child Left Behind, Chairman Alexander said the Education Department’s ‘supplement not supplant’ regulations “raises grave questions about what we might expect from future regulations.”

40.title: Alexander: Report Confirms Ed Dept. Proposal “Against the Law”
40.description:
Today, Senate education chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor after a nonpartisan government analysis confirmed the Dept. of Education’s proposed regulation is against the Every Student Succeeds Act, the new law fixing No Child Left Behind. 
Alexander said, “The United States Department of Education has apparently earned an "F" from the nonpartisan Congressional Research Service in its first attempt to write a regulation under the new law fixing No Child Left Behind that passed this body with 85 votes last year, that passed the House overwhelmingly and that President Obama signed into law in December calling it a Christmas miracle… It restored to the people closest to the children the authority for dealing with those children. Everybody wanted that. Virtually everybody wanted that except a few people in the United States Department of Education who can't keep their hands off America's 100,000 public schools… They are supposed to create an environment in which teachers and students and school boards can succeed. They're not supposed to serve as a national school board.”

41.title: Alexander Praises Bipartisan Bill Lower Student Loan Rates for 6.4M Undergrads
41.description: Today, Senate education chairman Lamar Alexander celebrated the news that student loan rates will drop from 4.29 percent to 3.76 percent, putting money back into the pockets of nearly 6.4 million undergraduate student borrowers. Alexander said the Bipartisan Student Loan Certainty Act of 2013, legislation he sponsored with Sens. King (I-Maine), Burr (R-N.C.), and Manchin (D-W.V.), “today reduces the rate by one half percent for nearly 6.4 million students and saves millions and millions and millions of dollars on student loans.”

42.title: Alexander Questions Sec. King On Ed Dept.’s Defining of Methodology for Supplement, not Supplant
42.description:
At this morning’s second oversight hearing on the new law fixing No Child Left Behind, Chairman Alexander questions Secretary King about the department’s negotiated rulemaking proposal on supplement not supplant, which Alexander said defined the methodology that local school districts must use—something specifically prohibited in the Every Student Succeeds Act. 

Alexander said, “What we put in the law, was that nothing in that section of the law supplement not supplant… shall be construed to authorize or permit the secretary to prescribe the specific methodology a local education agency uses. … In other words, we anticipated that you were going to try to not follow the law.”

43.title: Alexander: The effect of proposed rule is to change comparability law, which Congress did not change
43.description: Regarding a rule proposed by the Education Department in an April 1 negotiated rulemaking session, Chairman Alexander said to Secretary King “it is very clear that [Congress] did not intend that [the Education Department] come up with some clever way to use one provision, supplement not supplant, to change another provision, the comparability provision. … I hope you’ll take another look at that. Your responsibility is to faithfully execute the law and abide by the letter of the law, and I don’t think the beginning of those rule proposals suggest that some of the [department’s] employees are doing”

44.title: Alexander: Disturbing Evidence Dept. of Ed is Ignoring New Law to Fix NCLB
44.description: At this morning’s second oversight hearing on the new law fixing No Child Left Behind, Chairman Alexander told Education Secretary John King that  in a negotiated rulemaking session, “your department proposed a rule that would do exactly what the law says it shall not do …. Not only is what you’re doing against the law, the way you’re trying to do it is against another provision in the law.”

45.title: Collins: Proposed “NIHInnovation Fund” Matches NIH Priorities, Won’t Create Funding Cliff
45.description: At a Senate health appropriations subcommittee hearing this morning on the NIH FY17 budget request, NIH Director Dr. Francis Collins told Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander that Alexander’s proposed NIH Innovation Fund – to provide one-time targeted funding for Precision Medicine, Cancer Moonshot, Big Biothink Awards, Brain Initiative, and Young Investigator Corps—matches “major priorities” at the NIH and “would not result in a [funding] cliff.”

46.title: Alexander: Senate Companion to House “Cures” Will Be Most Important New Law This Year
46.description:
Today, the Senate health committee held its final markup on its biomedical innovation effort that will become the Senate companion to the 21st Century Cures Act – passed last year by the House of Representatives in a vote of 344-77.


Chairman Alexander said "Because our Innovation—or ‘Cures’—legislation will affect virtually every American, it will be the most important new law enacted this year...The House has done its work. The president has proposed his initiatives. I hopeful we can take this to the Senate floor soon and ensure the president’s Precision Medicine and cancer ‘moonshot’ initiatives and ideas in the ‘Cures’ bill can become reality this year.”

47.title: Alexander: Administration’s Overtime Rule Would Raise Tuition By $1,000 Per Student
47.description:
This morning at a Senate labor appropriations subcommittee hearing, Sen. Alexander asked Labor Dept. Secretary Thomas Perez about the department’s proposed overtime rule. Quoting a letter from a group of independent colleges in Tennessee, Alexander said, “One of our members calculated that the first year impact would translate to a $1,000 per student increase in tuition … It’s expected that the change will cost each four-year campus a minimum of $1. 3 million. Another rural campus noted the change would impact 133 employees for a total of 3.2 million dollars.”

Alexander, who chairs the Senate’s labor committee, then asked Perez that at a time when the administration talks about keeping “college costs down, how can you justify an overtime rule that might raise the cost of college by $1,000 per student?”

48.title: Alexander: “We Need an Education Secretary Confirmed by and Accountable to the United States Senate”
48.description: Senate education committee Chairman Alexander spoke on the floor urging the Senate to confirm Dr. John King Jr. as secretary of education, saying, “The reason we're voting today is that we need an education secretary … confirmed by and accountable to the United States Senate so that the law to fix No Child Left Behind will be implemented the way Congress wrote it."

49.title: Alexander Questions Acting Secretary Dr. King On Dept. of Education Use of Guidance
49.description: This morning at a hearing of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies, Senate education committee Chairman Lamar Alexander asked Dept. of Education  Acting Secretary John King about the Office for Civil Rights Assistant Secretary Catherine Lhamon’s treatment of guidance as legally binding in Title IX complaints without appropriate notice and comment. Illustrating the impact on colleges, Alexander said, “If I’m at small college out in Texas … I think she’s making the law, and I don’t dare not do what you want … You’ve changed the law for 6,000 colleges and universities.”

50.title: Alexander Asks King About Working Together to Simplify the FAFSA
50.description: This morning at a hearing of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies, Senate education committee Chairman Lamar Alexander asked Dept. of Education Acting Secretary John King about simplifying the federal student aid form, the FAFSA, which Alexander and a bipartisan group of senators have proposed to do through the FAST Act. Specifically, Alexander asked King for a list of the 30 questions the president has proposed eliminating in his budget, so Alexander and other senators could consider those items as they work to bring the form down from 108 questions to as close to two questions as possible.

51.title: Alexander Updates Senate On #Innovation2016 Agenda after 2nd Markup of Bipartisan Innovation Bills
51.description:
Today, Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor to update Americans on the Senate health committee's #Innovation2016 agenda. After the committee passed seven additional bipartisan bills. 
Sen. Alexander said, "The opportunity everybody wants us to take this year is to take advantage of this magnificent scientific revolution and encourage the research and the other steps we need to take to move treatments and cures and drugs into the medicine cabinets and the doctor's office more rapidly in a safe and effective way… I hope our work is finished by early April. I hope it is bipartisan, and I look forward to the opportunity of being able to say later this year that the most important bill that the Senate worked on with the House and the President is this 21st Century Cures idea.”

52.title: Alexander Says He Wants to Move Promptly to Get a Result on #Innovation2016 Agenda
52.description: Today, following the passage of seven more bipartisan biomedical innovation bills, Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander closed the second of three #Innovation2016 markups by saying “I think we can produce the most important bill of the Congress this year because our work on this bill will affect virtually every American—and  I look forward to doing it promptly so we can hand to Senator McConnell a conclusion to the innovation bill and on the surge of funding for NIH through mandatory funding in a bipartisan way, so he can put it on the floor. … I want to finish our work promptly, and I’ll be working with Senator Murray and other members of the committee to do that.”

53.title: Alexander: Biomedical Innovation Would be the Most Important Bill Signed into Law this Year
53.description:
Today, the Senate health committee held the second of three markups on biomedical innovation, considering seven bills with bipartisan support. 

Sen. Alexander said, “We’re in the middle of considering as many as 50 bipartisan proposals that we’ve been working on for more than a year. Our goal is to try to help America’s patients get access to safe drugs, devices, cures, and treatments more rapidly, as well as being safe and effective, which is the mission of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). … This year, the most important opportunity that everybody wants to take advantage of is this remarkable scientific opportunity in biomedical research. It offers the promise of help for virtually every American. And I believe if we would succeed, it will be the most important piece of legislation signed into law this year.”

54.title: Alexander Questions King On The Role Of The Department Of Education
54.description: In a second round of questions at today’s hearing on the president's nominee for Education Secretary, Senate education committee Chairman Alexander asked nominee Dr. John King about specific prohibitions on the role of the Department of Education and how Dr. King would work with Alexander on reducing burdensome higher education regulations.

55.title: Alexander Questions King on Timing for Implementation of New Law to Fix No Child Left Behind
55.description: At today's hearing on the president's nominee for Education Secretary, Senate education committee Chairman Alexander asked nominee Dr. John King about the timing of department regulations and when new state plans to be submitted.

56.title: Alexander to King: If Confirmed, I’ll Work with You to Implement NCLB Fix “as Congress Wrote It”
56.description: At today's hearing on the president's nominee for Education Secretary, Senate education committee Chairman Alexander told nominee Dr. John King that the Senate will work with him to implement the bipartisan law fixing No Child Left Behind "as Congress wrote it."

57.title: Alexander Questions Administration Witnesses on Zika Transmission and Diagnostic Testing
57.description: This morning at the Senate health committee hearing on the Zika virus, Chairman Alexander questioned National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases Director Dr. Anthony Fauci and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Principal Deputy Director Dr. Anne Schuchat on what Americans who are concerned about the Zika virus need to know about transmission and diagnostic testing.

58.title: Alexander Holds Health Committee Hearing to Seek Updates on Zika Virus
58.description: Today Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander held a hearing to seek updates on the public health threat posed by the Zika virus and on progress in developing vaccines and diagnostic tests.

59.title: Alexander: Federal Govt. is Prohibited from Mandating Common Core Under New Law to Fix NCLB
59.description: At this morning’s first oversight hearing on the new law fixing No Child Left Behind, Chairman Alexander talks with State Superintendent of Public Instruction at the Wisconsin Department of Public Instruction Dr. Tony Evers about how federal government is explicitly prohibited from reviewing state standards and incentivising the adoption of the Common Core standards.

60.title: Senate Education Committee Holds First Every Student Succeeds Act Oversight Hearing
60.description:
Today, the Senate education committee held its first oversight hearing on the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA), the new law fixing No Child Left Behind. Chairman Lamar Alexander said "a law not properly implemented isn’t worth the paper it’s printed on." 
 
This is the first of six hearings the committee will hold this year to make sure that the law is being implemented in the way that Congress wrote it.

61.title: Alexander Talks Implementation of New Law Fixing No Child Left Behind with Hearing Witnesses
61.description: At this morning’s first oversight hearing on the new law fixing No Child Left Behind, Chairman Alexander talks with witnesses Utah Governor Gary Herbert,  American Federation of Teachers President Randi Weingarten and National Education Association Vice President Becky Pringle about forming state coalitions to help implement the Every Student Succeeds Act.

62.title: Alexander urges senators to support Dr. Califf’s nomination to head the FDA
62.description: Today, Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor in support of Dr. Robert Califf to lead the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Alexander said, “Dr. Califf's nomination comes at an important time for the FDA,” noting that the agency “needs a confirmed commissioner to provide the leadership that will carry the agency into the future.”

63.title: Alexander: Going To Focus "On Making Sure That #ESSA Is Being Implemented In The Way We Wrote It."
63.description:
Today on the Senate floor, Chairman Alexander talked about a letter from the governors, superintendents, principals and others to Acting Secretary of the Department of Education John King regarding implementation of the Every Student Succeeds Act.  He read part of their letter on the Senate floor saying, "The new law replaces a top-down accountability and testing regime with an inclusive system based on collaborative state and local innovation. For this vision to become a reality, we must work together to closely honor congressional intent: ESSA is clear. Education decision-making now rests with states and districts, and the federal role is to support and inform those decisions." 

The Senate education committee plans to hold six oversight hearing on ESSA throughout this year.

64.title: Alexander Questions Administration Witnesses on What Americans Need to Know About the  Zika Virus
64.description: This morning at a hearing of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies, Sen. Alexander questioned Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Director Dr. Frieden and National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases Director Dr. Fauci on what Americans who are concerned about the Zika virus need to know—as well as on the status of a vaccine.

65.title: Alexander Discusses Beginning of HELP Committee’s #Innovation2016 Initiative on Senate Floor
65.description: On the Senate floor, Senate health committee Chairman Alexander discussed yesterday’s successful committee meeting in which seven biomedical innovation bills were passed with bipartisan support. He said, “Last year we worked together despite our differences of opinion and produced a bill to fix No Child Left Behind. A lot of people thought we couldn't do that. … We have a second markup of legislation scheduled for March 9 and a third for April 6. And my expectation is that after we meet these three times and consider 50 legislative proposals, it will all add up to bipartisan companion legislation to the House's 21st Century Cures legislation, and that our legislation will include important elements of the president's Precision Medicine Initiative in his cancer moonshot. Alexander explained his idea of creating a "NIH Innovation Projects Fund," which he described as “five areas in addition to the things that we normally fund, that require extraordinary support – onetime support – ideas that have a start and a finish. In other words, they're not built into the budget for a long period of time. The NIH Director would have the authority to direct allocations of this fund to specific areas of importance.” Alexander then listed the five areas he had in mind: 1. The president's Precision Medicine Initiative; 2. a Young Investigators Corps; 3. the BRAIN initiative; 4. Big BioThink Awards; 5. the cancer moonshot.

66.title: Alexander Says An EHR System That Works is Essential to #Innovation2016
66.description: Today at its first #Innovation2016 markup, the Senate health committee passed Chairman Alexander and Ranking Member Murray's legislation to improve health information technology for doctors and their patients.

67.title: Senate Health Committee Considers First Series of #Innovation2016 Bills
67.description:
Today, the Senate health committee held the first of three markups on biomedical innovation, considering seven bills with bipartisan support. 

Of the committee’s #Innovation2016 agenda, Chairman Alexander has said “the House has completed its work on the 21st Century Cures Act. The president has announced his support for a precision medicine initiative and a cancer ‘moonshot.’ It is urgent that the Senate finish its work and turn into law these ideas that will help virtually every American.”

68.title: Alexander Questions FDA Witness Dr. Janet Woodcock on Backlog of Generic Drug Approvals
68.description: Chairman Alexander questions Director at the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research at FDA Dr. Janet Woodcock on why the median approval time of generic drugs has slowed from 30 to 48 months despite an extra $1 billion in funding.

69.title: Alexander Holds Oversight Hearing on Slowdown of FDA Generic Drug Approva
69.description: Chairman Alexander today held an oversight hearing on of the generic drug user fee program. Alexander said that despite the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) receiving an extra $1 billion to speed up approvals, the agency’s approval pace has slowed and “these slower approval times mean less competition and higher costs for consumers.”

70.title: Alexander Asks How States Can Most Effectively Spend on Mental Health Programs
70.description: Chairman Alexander asks National Association of State Mental Health Program Directors Executive Director Brian Hepburn, MD, where he thinks states should focus spending on mental health services.

71.title: Alexander Discusses With Witnesses How To Help People With Mental Illness
71.description: Chairman Alexander discusses best practices on how to help those with mental illness get the care they need with Live Breathe CEO Hakeem Rahim, EdM, MA and Professor William W. Eaton, PhD, from the Department of Mental Health at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health

72.title: Alexander Says Committee Plans to "Move Promptly" on Mental Health Recommendations
72.description: Today Chairman Alexander opened the first Senate health committee hearing on mental health in 2016 by saying the committee plans to “move promptly” to offer bipartisan recommendations to help address the mental health crisis affecting about one in five American adults.

73.title: Alexander Leads Senate Floor Discussion On Perkins Loan Compromise
73.description: Today, Chairman Alexander led a discussion on the Senate floor with Senators Ayotte, Baldwin, Portman, and Casey on their Perkins Loans Program compromise, which provides a two-year extension of the program while the Senate education committee works to reauthorize the Higher Education Act and find a long-term solution for students that makes it simpler and easier to apply for financial aid and afford college.

74.title: Alexander Speaks After ESSA Is Sent To the President By A Vote Of 85-12
74.description:
Caption: 
After the Senate passed the Every Student Succeeds Act 85-12, Chairman Alexander said he hopes “President Obama will wrap a big red bow around it and sign it” for 50 million children and 3.4 million teachers in 100,000 public schools.

75.title: Alexander on ESSA: We’ve Come To A Good Conclusion For 50 Million Students
75.description: Ahead of the Senate vote on final passage of the Every Student Succeeds Act, Chairman Alexander said, “The United States Senate, [the House of Representatives]—and, I believe, the president by the end of the week—will have a Christmas present for 50 million children and 3.4 million teachers in 100,000 public schools across this country—something they’ve been eagerly awaiting.”

76.title: Alexander Questions Witnesses on Differences in Opioid Abuse Treatments
76.description: Chairman Lamar Alexander discusses different treatments for opioid abuse with Eric Spofford, CEO of Granite House, Dr. Leana Wen, Baltimore City health commissioner, and Dr. Robert Valuck, professor in the Department of Clinical Pharmacy at the University of Colorado.

77.title: Alexander Says GOP Senate Kept Promise To Repeal Common Core Mandate
77.description: Sen. Alexander joins Majority Leader McConnell and Senate Republican leadership to talk about the Every Student Succeeds Act, which fixes No Child Left Behind, ends the federal Common Core mandate, and restores local education control

78.title: Alexander Encourages All Senators To Vote In Support of Cloture on ESSA
78.description: Ahead of the Senate cloture vote on the Every Student Succeeds Act, Chairman Alexander encouraged all senators to vote in favor of ending debate and moving on to final passage to fix the “law that everybody wants to fix,” No Child Left Behind.

79.title: Alexander Holds HELP Hearing On Combating Growing Epidemic of Opioid Abuse
79.description: Health committee Chair Lamar Alexander opens Senate hearing on combating the growing, nationwide epidemic of opioid abuse. He said, “The human costs of this epidemic are too high, and I hear about the challenges of dealing with this epidemic at home in Tennessee, particularly in East Tennessee where I am from. ...[b]ut, the truth is, this problem affects all states and is frontline issue for communities all over.”

80.title: Alexander Leads Members of Senate HELP Committee in Colloquy on Negative Consequences of Obamacare
80.description: Chairman Alexander today spoke on the Senate floor, joined by Senate health committee members, Sens. Isakson and Cassidy, to discuss the negative impacts Obamacare. From Tennessee to Georgia and Louisiana, the senators shared stories of how real Americans have been negatively affected by rising premiums, reduced working hours, and fewer choices of plans.

81.title: Alexander Calls Obamacare “an Historic Mistake” As Debate On Repeal Legislation Begins
81.description: Today on the Senate floor, Chairman Alexander laid out what Republicans warned the president would happen if Obamacare became law, including higher premiums, increased taxes, and lost jobs. He urged the president and Senate Democrats to work with Republicans to fix the damage Obamacare has done to health care and pass real reforms that lower costs so more Americans can afford to buy insurance.

82.title: Alexander Delivers Opening Remarks at First Conference Cmte. Meeting to Fix No Child Left Behind
82.description: Today, Chairman Alexander opened the first House and Senate conference meeting on fixing No Child Left Behind by saying: “There are a lot of people counting on us to get a result: 50 million children and 3.4 million teachers in 100,000 public schools.”

83.title: Alexander Questions Califf on Generic Drug Approval Wait Times, FDA Use of Guidance
83.description:
At today’s HELP Committee hearing on the nomination of Dr. Robert Califf to head the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Chairman Alexander questioned Califf on why the backlog for generic drug approvals has increased—despite the FDA receiving about 1 billion in new funds over the last three years.  

Alexander also asked for assurance Califf would look into the FDA’s issuing of guidance instead of going through the rulemaking process.

84.title: Alexander Opens HELP Committee Hearing to Consider Nomination of Dr. Califf to Lead FDA
84.description: At today’s hearing on the nomination of Dr. Robert Califf to head the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Chairman Alexander said he looks forward to hearing how Califf will “help ensure that affordable drugs are available to American patients." Specifically, Alexander asked how the "FDA can help the market lower drug prices by approving generic drugs and other products as quickly as it possibly can, so there is more choice and competition in the market.”

85.title: Alexander Questions Administration Witness On NIH Research Findings
85.description: Chairman Alexander questions Dr. Tom Insel, M.D., Director at the National Institute of Mental Health at the National Institutes of Health, on recent findings in schizophrenia and brain research.

86.title: Alexander Discusses Relationship Between Smoking & Mental Health with Hearing Witness
86.description: Chairman Alexander discusses with Dr. Tom Insel, M.D., Director of National Institute of Mental Health the relationship between smoking and mental health.

87.title: Chairman Alexander Opens Hearing On Priorities, Challenges, and Oppourutnites in Mental Health

88.title: Chairman Alexander On Floor: Obama Should ‘Stop and Think’ On Over-Testing Problem

89.title: Alexander Questions Dr. Francis Collins, Director at NIH
89.description: At a Senate Committee on Appropriations Subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies Hearing, Senator Alexander questioned National Institutes of Health Director Francis Collins,  M.D., Ph.D. on whether there was a justification for having a steadier stream of mandatory funding, such as for preventive or precision medicine.

90.title: Alexander Questions Mark Kisicki on OSHA’s and other agencies’ Use of Joint Employer Standard
90.description: Alexander asked Mark Kisicki, shareholder at Ogletree Deakins, Nash, Smoak & Stewart P.C., “Why do you suppose OSHA is going around trying to figure out if some employer is a joint employer, when it’s job is really worker safety?”

91.title: Alexander: Closing Remarks on Labor Committee Hearing On NLRB's Joint Employer Standard

92.title: Alexander Questions MODE Stores Founder Ciara Stockeland
92.description: At Senate labor committee hearing on the NLRB’s new joint employer standard, Chairman Alexander asks Ciara Stockeland, owner and founder of MODE Stores, if she would have been able to expand to 11 stores without franchising. Alexander asked Stockeland, “Would you have been able to grow so quickly without relying on the franchisee model?”

93.title: Sen. Alexander Questions Mark Kisicki at HELP Hearing on NLRB’s New Joint Employer Standard
93.description: Senate labor committee Chairman Alexander questions Mark Kisicki, a shareholder at Ogletree Deakins, Nash, Smoak & Stewart, asking him how he would advise a business that has franchised its brand and wanted to avoid potential liabilities resulting from the National Labor Relations Board’s new joint employer decision.

94.title: Alexander Calls on Democrats to Help Reverse NLRB Joint-Employer Decision
94.description: As chairman of the Senate labor committee, Alexander today urged Senate Democrats to support legislation to roll back a recent National Labor Relations Board decision he said may “steal the American dream from owners of the nation’s 780,000 franchise businesses and millions of contractors.”

95.title: Senator Alexander Discusses Perkins Loan Program on Senate Floor Part II

96.title: Alexander Questions Dept. of Health & Human Services Witnesses at 6th HELP Committee Hearing on EHRs
96.description: Sen. Alexander questions Dr. Karen DeSalvo, National Coordinator for Health Information Technology in the Department of Health and Human Services, and Dr. Patrick Conway, Acting Principal Deputy Administrator and Deputy Administrator for Innovation and Quality at the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services, on taking more time before making final the Stage 3 rule for the electronic health records program. Alexander asked Conway, “Why don’t you … work with doctors, hospitals and vendors and make your changes [to Stage 3] before you make it final?”

97.title: Alexander: Closing Remarks at HELP Hearing on Health Information Technology

98.title: Alexander Gives 5 Reasons To Delay Making Final Stage 3 Rule for EHR Program
98.description: “The whole purpose of this program is to benefit patients, so that they and their health care providers have quicker and better access to their health histories and their doctors and hospitals and pharmacists can provide them with better care,” Alexander told administration witnesses at today’s hearing, the committee’s sixth on electronic health records.

99.title: Senator Alexander Discusses Perkins Loan Program on Senate Floor -- 9.30.15

100.title: Alexander Questions Dept. of Labor Witness at HSGAC Hearing on Regulatory Guidance
100.description: Senator Alexander questions Ms. Mary Beth Maxwell, Principal deputy assistant secretary for policy for the Department of Labor, about the department’s use of guidance.

101.title: Alexander Questions Dept. of Ed. Witness at HSGAC Hearing on Regulatory Guidance
101.description: Senator Alexander questions Ms. Amy McIntosh, deputy assistant secretary for the Department of Education, about the department’s use of guidance.

102.title: Alexander Calls for Delay of Making Final Rules for Stage Three of Electronic Health Records Program
102.description: Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) today called for a delay until January 1, 2017, of making final rules for stage three of the federal government’s program to require doctors and hospitals to create electronic health records systems.

103.title: Alexander Closing Remarks at Higher Ed Hearing on Opportunities for Student Success

104.title: Alexander Questions Witnesses at Higher Ed Hearing on Opportunities for Student Success

105.title: Alexander: Federal Policies Should Encourage Students to Complete College on Time
105.description: U.S. Senate education committee Chairman Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) today said federal aid policies should encourage students to make progress in college and complete on time, and higher education policies should help colleges and universities help their students finish their degree or certificate.

106.title: Alexander: Info Blocking is Standing in Way of Patients, Promise of EHRs
