106.description: WASHINGTON, D.C., July 23 – Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) today chaired a hearing on the practice of “information blocking”—when something or someone creates an obstacle to the electronic sharing of a person’s health information—and raised the question of whether the federal government, through its program to encourage adoption of electronic health records, played a role in encouraging the practice.

107.title: Alexander Amendment Would Provide 11 Million $2,100 “Scholarships for Kids”
107.description:
WASHINGTON, D.C., July 8 – Senate education committee Chairman Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) today offered an amendment to the bill being debated by the Senate to fix No Child Left Behind that would allow $2,100 federal scholarships to follow 11 million low-income children to any public or private accredited school of their parents’ choice.  

“Equal opportunity in America should mean that everyone has the same starting line,” Alexander said. “There would be no better way to help children move up from the back of the line than by allowing states to use federal dollars to create 11 million new opportunities to choose a better school.”

108.title: Alexander: Senate Begins Debate on Bipartisan Bill to Fix NCLB, a “Law That Everyone Wants to Fix”
108.description:
As the United States Senate today began debate on his bipartisan bill to fix No Child Left Behind, Chairman Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) today said the bill reflects the shared belief by both Democrats and Republicans that lawmakers should respect the judgments of those closest to the children “and leave to them most decisions about how to help 3.4 million teachers help 50 million children in 100,000 public schools improve student achievement.”

Alexander said: “Newsweek Magazine this week called this the ‘law that everyone wants to fix.’ There’s broad consensus about that. And remarkably, there’s also consensus about how to fix it. That consensus is this: that we should continue the law’s important measurements of students’ academic progress but restore to states, school districts, classroom teachers, and parents the responsibility for deciding what to do about the results of these measurements. 

He added: “This change should produce fewer tests and more appropriate ways to measure student achievement. We believe this is the most effective path toward higher standards, better teaching and real accountability.

109.title: Alexander Questions Witnesses at Hearing to Identify Solutions to EHR Program
109.description: Senate health committee chairman Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) today chaired the first in a series of hearings intended to solve problems with the federal government’s six-year-old, $30 billion program meant to encourage adoption of electronic health records at doctor’s offices and hospitals.

110.title: Alexander on Institutional Risk Sharing
110.description: At today's hearing on "Reauthorizing the Higher Education Act: Exploring Institutional Risk-sharing," Senate education Chairman Lamar Alexander questioned witnesses about ways to help encourage colleges and universities to help students reduce their overborrowing and complete college more quickly, as well as ways to urge colleges to be more efficient with costs so tuition rises more slowly.

111.title: Alexander to EEOC: Agency with Critical Task Has Gotten Far Afield of Mission
111.description: At today's hearing on "Oversight of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission: Examining the EEOC's Enforcement and Litigation Programs," Senate labor committee Chairman Lamar Alexander told the chair and general counsel of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission that he is concerned the agency is pursuing investigations with no complaints while the backlog of complaints grows, receiving embarrassing court rebukes, and seems to be inventing ways to avoid following the law.

112.title: Alexander Presses NLRB Chairman About Board's Latest Move that Undermines Right-to-Work Law
112.description: At an appropriations subcommittee hearing today on the president’s budget request for the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB), Senate labor committee Chairman Lamar Alexander pressed NLRB Chairman Mark Pearce about the board’s recent request for legal briefs to determine if unions in right-to-work states can force employees, who work in a unionized workplace but have chosen not to join the union, to pay union dues and fees. Alexander said the board’s request for “briefs on laws that have been settled for 40 years suggests that the board is thinking about undermining a state like Tennessee’s ability to have a right-to-work law.”

113.title: Alexander Questions Witnesses at Hearing on Reauthorizing Higher Education
113.description: At today's hearing on the reauthorization of the Higher Education Act: "Reauthorizing the Higher Education Act: The Role of Consumer Information in College Choice," Senate education committee Chairman Lamar Alexander questioned witnesses about ways to improve financial aid data collection and the benefits of providing students with their financial aid eligibility information in their junior year in high school rather than their senior year.

114.title: Alexander Holds Higher Education Hearing on "The Role of Consumer Information in College Choice"
114.description: Senate education committee Chairman Lamar Alexander today led the committee's second hearing this Congress on the reauthorization of the Higher Education Act: "Reauthorizing the Higher Education Act: The Role of Consumer Information in College Choice."

115.title: Alexander: Failing Electronic Health Records Program May Stand in Way of Precision Medicine
115.description: At today's hearing on "Realizing the Promise of Precision Medicine for Patients," Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander said that the “failed promise” of the $28 billion electronic health records program may stand in the way of a precision medicine initiative until physicians are able to use systems that communicate with one another.

116.title: Alexander Questions Witnesses at HELP Committee Hearing on Precision Medicine
116.description: At today's hearing on "Realizing the Promise of Precision Medicine for Patients," Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander asked witnesses to work with the HELP committee to identify five or six steps needed to get our country's medical records system functioning so that it supports precision medicine, and is "something that physicians and providers can looking forward to using instead of enduring."

117.title: Chairman Alexander: Closing Remarks at Third HELP Committee Hearing on FDA and NIH Innovation

118.title: Alexander Questions Witnesses at Third HELP Committee Hearing on FDA and NIH Innovation

119.title: Alexander: FDA and NIH Must be Ready for the Medical Breakthroughs that are Coming
119.description: Senate health Committee Chairman Lamar Alexander today urged experts from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to help Congress in its work to ensure that “the exciting new technologies being developed and discoveries being made are reaching patients-- that the NIH is equipped to support the early-stage research required to make these advancements and that the FDA is equipped to review them.”

120.title: Alexander Questions HHS Sec. Burwell at Hearing on President's 2016 HHS Budget Request
120.description: At the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Labor-Health and Human Services today, Senate labor committee Chairman Lamar Alexander today asked U.S. Dept. of Health and Human Services Secretary Sylvia Burwell if she will commit to working with Congress to make "electronic health records something that physicians and providers look forward to instead of something they endure."

121.title: Alexander on Unanimous Committee Passage of Bipartisan Agreement to Fix No Child Left Behind
121.description: Senate education committee Chairman Lamar Alexander today praised the work of the committee in acting on the bipartisan agreement to fix No Child Left Behind. After three days of amendment and debate, the committee voted unanimously to send the bill to the full Senate. Alexander said the consensus that the committee found is to "continue the law’s important measurements of academic progress of students but restore to states, school districts, classroom teachers and parents the responsibility for deciding what to do about improving student achievement."

122.title: Alexander on Bipartisan Legislative Agreement to Fix No Child Left Behind
122.description: At the start of the Senate education committee markup today of bipartisan legislation to fix No Child Left Behind, Chairman Lamar Alexander said the bill reflects “remarkable consensus” about how to fix the problems with the law. Alexander said the agreement will "continue the law’s important measurements of academic progress of students but restore to states, school districts, classroom teachers and parents the responsibility for deciding what to do about improving student achievement.  This change should produce fewer tests and more appropriate ways to measure student achievement."

123.title: Alexander Questions Witnesses at Second Hearing on FDA, NIH Innovation
123.description: At today’s hearing, "Continuing America's Leadership: Advancing Research and Development for Patients," Alexander questioned the panel of witnesses, asking for their thoughts on the impact of administrative burdens on innovation and research.

124.title: Alexander's Closing Remarks at Second Hearing on FDA, NIH Innovation

125.title: Alexander: NIH and FDA Must Keep Pace with Today’s Cutting-edge Scientific Advances
125.description: At the second hearing on the committee’s bipartisan initiative to examine the process for getting medical products through discovery and development into medicine cabinets, Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander today told the story of 3-year-old Tennessean whose struggle with cystic fibrosis “illustrates why we’re embarking on this effort and why it’s so important for us to get a result.”

126.title: Alexander Questions Witnesses at HELP Hearing on America's Health IT Transformation
126.description: Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander questions a panel of witnesses about using “meaningful use” programs to provide more effective care for patients at today's hearing, "America's Health IT Transformation: Translating the Promise of Electronic Health Records Into Better Care."

127.title: Alexander Questions Witnesses at HELP Hearing on America's Health IT Transformation
127.description: Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander questions a panel of witnesses about using “meaningful use” programs to provide more effective care for patients at today's hearing, "America's Health IT Transformation: Translating the Promise of Electronic Health Records Into Better Care."

128.title: HELP Chairman Alexander Holds Hearing on America's Health IT System
128.description: Today Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander held a hearing titled, "America's Health IT Transformation: Translating the Promise of Electronic Health Records Into Better Care." In the first Senate health committee hearing on Health IT since the 2009 passage of HITECH Act, Chairman Alexander discussed electronic health records and examined why goals for “meaningful use” program have not yet been reached.

129.title: Alexander's Closing Remarks at Hearing on Bipartisan Initiative to Examine Drug, Device Development

130.title: Alexander Questions FDA Commissioner, NIH Director at Hearing on U.S. Drug, Device Development
130.description: At today’s hearing, “Continuing America’s Leadership in Medical Innovation for Patients,” Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander questions FDA Commissioner Margaret Hamburg and NIH Director Francis Collins about ways to improve our country's biomedical research and development.

131.title: Alexander Chairs Hearing On Bipartisan Initiative to Examine Drug & Device Development Process
131.description: Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander today held a hearing titled, “Continuing America’s Leadership in Medical Innovation for Patients,” on the committee's bipartisan initiative to “examine how we get drugs, devices and treatments from the discovery process through the regulatory process into our medicine cabinets and doctors’ offices.” In January, Alexander released the “Innovation for Healthier Americans” report with Senator Richard Burr that identified 5 issues with the process the U.S. has in place today for drug and device development.

132.title: Alexander: Ending the NLRB Rule Would Return Fairness, Balance to Employer & Employee Relationships
132.description: Senate labor committee Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor this afternoon after the Senate agreed on the motion to proceed to the Congressional Review Act resolution of disapproval for the National Labor Relations Board's (NRLB) ambush election rule. Alexander said stopping the board's rule would return "fairness and balance back to the relationship between employers and employees in this country."

133.title: Alexander on Senate Vote to Proceed to Congressional Review Act to Stop NLRB's Ambush Election Rule
133.description: Senate labor committee Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor this afternoon after the Senate voted to proceed to the Congressional Review Act resolution of disapproval for the National Labor Relations Board's (NLRB) ambush election rule. The Senate agreed on the motion to proceed to the resolution, which was introduced in the Senate by Alexander with Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell and Senator Mike Enzi last month, by a vote 53-45.

134.title: Chairman Alexander’s Remarks at Hearing on Medical and Public Health Preparedness and Response
134.description: At today's hearing, "Medical and Public Health Preparedness and Response: Are We Ready for Future Threats?", Senator Alexander called on the administration to ensure someone is “on the flagpole” during future health threats—citing confusion over who was in charge during the “near panic in the United States over Ebola.” He then asked Dr. Robinson, the Deputy Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response and Director of the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, if there is anything Congress can do that would help researchers who are developing ways to prevent or ‎treat both identified and emerging threats.

135.title: Alexander on Ebola and Medical and Public Health Preparedness

136.title: Alexander: Task Force Report is a “Blueprint for How We Can Reduce Overregulation” of Higher Ed
136.description: Senate education committee Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor today about deregulating higher education, where he said a bipartisan task force report finding colleges in a jungle of red tape shows “sloppy, inefficient governing that wastes money, hurts students, discourages productivity and impedes research.” Alexander said this report will serve as a "blueprint for how we can reduce overregulation, simplify rules, save money, make consumer protection clear, keep tuition down, find more money for research, and let colleges and universities spend their time and money educating students instead of filling out forms."

137.title: Alexander Questions Witnesses on Findings of Task Force Report on Deregulating Higher Education
137.description: At the first hearing this Congress on the reauthorization of the Higher Education Act, Senate education committee Chairman Alexander discusses reducing government regulations of higher education with Chancellors Nicholas Zeppos of Vanderbilt University and William Kirwan of the University of Maryland.

138.title: Alexander: Bipartisan Report Finds Colleges in a Jungle of Red Tape
138.description: At the first hearing this Congress on the reauthorization of the Higher Education Act, Senate education committee Chairman Lamar Alexander said a report released by a task force of college and university leaders—and commissioned by a bipartisan group of senators, including Alexander—shows colleges in a jungle of red tape that “should be an embarrassment to all of us in the federal government.”

139.title: Alexander Asks Questions to Hearing Witnesses Regarding the NLRB’s Ambush Election Rule
139.description: Senate labor committee Chairman Lamar Alexander asks questions of the witness panel regarding the NLRB's ambush election rule and its impact on businesses at today's hearing, "Ambushed: How the NLRB's New Election Rule Harms Employers & Employees."

140.title: Alexander: NLRB’s Ambush Election Rule “Will Harm Employers and Employees Alike”
140.description: At today's hearing on the National Labor Relations Board's ambush election rule, Senate labor committee Chairman Lamar Alexander said this rule, issued by the board in December to speed up union elections, will “harm employers and employees alike.”

141.title: Alexander Questions Witnesses at HELP Hearing on Vaccines
141.description: Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander questions a panel of witnesses, including Dr. Kelly Moore of the Tennessee Department of Health in Nashville, about the Measles outbreak at today's hearing, "The Reemergence of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases: Exploring the Public Health Successes and Challenges."

142.title: Alexander Questions Dr. Anne Schuchat of CDC at HELP Hearing on Vaccines
142.description: Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander today asked Dr. Anne Schuchat, director of the National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, about the Measles outbreak and why parents are choosing not to vaccinate their children at today's hearing, "The Reemergence of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases: Exploring the Public Health Successes and Challenges."

143.title: Alexander: Vaccines Save Lives
143.description: At today's hearing on the re-emergence of vaccine-preventable diseases, Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander said: “From smallpox to polio, we have learned in the United States that vaccines save lives.  And yet a troubling number of parents are not vaccinating their children.”

144.title: Alexander, McConnell, Enzi Speak on Joint Resolution to Stop NLRB Ambush Election Rule
144.description: Today, Senate labor committee Chairman Lamar Alexander, Majority Leader Mitch McConnell (R-Ky.) and Sen. Mike Enzi (R-Wyo.) spoke on the Senate floor about the joint resolution they issued through the Congressional Review Act with Representatives John Kline and Phil Roe that would stop the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) from implementing its “ambush election” rule.

145.title: Alexander: NLRB Decision “Could Destroy a Small Business Opportunity for Over 700,000 Americans”
145.description: Senate labor committee Chairman Lamar Alexander today asked questions to hearing witnesses about the pending National Labor Relations Board decision to change the joint employer standard, which Alexander says “could destroy a small business opportunity for more than 700,000 Americans.”

146.title: Alexander: Federal Dollars Should Enable and Encourage—Not Mandate—State, Local K-12 Innovation
146.description: At a roundtable on fixing No Child Left Behind today, Senate education committee Chairman Lamar Alexander said the federal government ought to be an enabler and encourager, rather than a mandater, of state and local K-12 innovation.

147.title: Alexander on "Innovation for Healthier Americans" Report
147.description: Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander spoke on the Senate floor this afternoon on the “Innovation for Healthier Americans” report he and Senator Burr released today. The senators' report details the challenges to getting safe treatments, devices and cures to patients more quickly and effectively, examining what is working, and what isn’t, at the Food and Drug Administration and the National Institutes of Health.

148.title: Alexander: EEOC General Counsel’s Actions May Discourage Employers from Using Wellness Programs
148.description: At a Senate health committee hearing on employee wellness programs today, Chairman Lamar Alexander said that actions taken by the general counsel of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission may discourage employers from using a tool authorized by Obamacare to lower employees’ health care costs.

149.title: Education Chairman Alexander Questions Witnesses at Hearing on Fixing No Child Left Behind
149.description: Senate education committee Chairman Lamar Alexander asks a series of questions on teacher evaluation to a panel of witnesses at today's hearing, "Fixing No Child Left Behind: Supporting Teachers and School Leaders."

150.title: Alexander: Washington Telling States How to Evaluate Teachers Has Caused “Enormous Backlash”
150.description: Senate education committee chairman Lamar Alexander today said Washington must encourage—but not mandate—teacher and principal evaluation systems if they want to improve the nation’s 100,000 public schools.

151.title: Alexander: Restoring Full-time to 40 Hours Could Give 2.6 Million Workers a Pay Raise
151.description: Senate health committee Chairman Lamar Alexander today said the Senate should change the Obamacare definition of full-time from 30 hours to 40 and give “as many as 2.6 million workers a pay raise.”

152.title: Chairman Alexander's Closing Remarks at Committee Hearing on No Child Left Behind

153.title: Chairman Alexander Questions Panelists at Committee Hearing on No Child Left Behind

154.title: Alexander Questions Witnesses About Testing and School Accountability
154.description: Chairman Alexander questions witnesses about school testing and accountability at today's Senate education committee hearing on No Child Left Behind.

155.title: Alexander Leads Hearing on Fixing No Child Left Behind: Testing and Accountability
155.description:
U.S. Sen. Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) today gaveled in his first hearing as chairman of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, calling for the committee to pass a bipartisan bill to Fix No Child Left Behind by the end of February.
 
“Almost everyone seems to agree that it’s time to fix No Child Left Behind—it’s more than 7 years overdue.  We’ve been working on it for more than 6 years, we’ve had 24 hearings, and in each of the last two Congresses we’ve reported bills out of committee. Twenty of 22 senators on this committee were members in the last congress, and 16 of these 22 were here in the previous congress.”

156.title: Education Chairman Alexander Announces Plan for Fixing No Child Left Behind

157.title: Alexander Introduces FAST Act to Simplify Student Aid Application
157.description: Sen. Alexander introduced the FAST Act on the Senate floor today, authored by Alexander and Sen. Bennet (D-Colo.) and joined by Sens. Richard Burr (R-N.C.), Booker (D-N.J.), Isakson (R-Ga.), and King (I- Maine). The FAST Act would simplify the process of applying for and receiving federal financial aid to attend college, allow year-round use of Pell Grants, discourage over-borrowing and simplify repayments.

158.title: Alexander Questions NLRB Nominee McFerran on the Joint-Employer Standard
158.description: Sen. Alexander questions National Labor Relations Board nominee Lauren McFerran about the joint-employer standard, urging her to carefully consider the extent to which the franchisor should be held liable for the unfair labor practices of the local franchisee, if appointed as a member of the board.

159.title: Alexander on McFerran's Nomination to the NLRB
159.description: Sen. Alexander today delivered remarks at the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee hearing on the nomination of Lauren McFerran to serve as a Member of The National Labor Relations Board.

160.title: Alexander on the Child Care & Development Block Grant
160.description: Ahead of tonight’s vote on the Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG) Act of 2014, Sen. Alexander spoke on the Senate floor regarding the legislation he cosponsored to help approximately 900,000 families across the country access safe, affordable child care.

161.title: Alexander on the Child Care & Development Block Grant
161.description: Ahead of this afternoon’s cloture vote, Alexander spoke on the Senate floor and told the success story of a Memphis mother who received a child care voucher through this program. Her young child received care while she got her degree and rose to an assistant manager at Walmart, and she is now able to pay for child care for her second child without help from the federal government. “This is exactly the kind of legislating we should be doing at the federal level,” Alexander said. “It follows the example of other successful federal programs by enabling American families to help themselves.”

162.title: Alexander Says ABLE Act Will Remove Federal Barriers for Individuals with Disabilities
162.description: At a hearing today, U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) said passing the ABLE Act will remove federal barriers for nearly 9,500 individuals with disabilities in Knox County—allowing them to earn and save money without losing federal benefits.

163.title: Alexander says Threat of Ebola Must be Taken as Seriously as ISIS
163.description: In a joint hearing today between the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee and Senate Appropriations Committee, U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) spoke about the major risk posed by Ebola if it is not met by a "huge and immediate response."

164.title: On CNN: Sen. Alexander Calls for Urgent Response to Ebola Epidemic
164.description: In an interview this afternoon with CNN's Wolf Blitzer, Sen. Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) discussed the importance of a serious, urgent response to the Ebola epidemic.

165.title: Alexander Introduces “NLRB Reform Act” to Change the National Labor Relations Board from an
165.description: U.S. Sen. Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) today introduced the NLRB Reform Act to turn the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) from an advocate to an umpire in labor disputes. Alexander introduced the legislation with Senate Republican Leader Mitch McConnell (R-Ky.).

166.title: Alexander: Obama Labor Board Nominee Has Caused “Mess of Confusion” for Tenn. Workers, Businesses
166.description: U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate labor committee, today told President Obama’s nominee for the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB), Sharon Block, that her previous unconstitutional appointment created “a mess of confusion” for Tennessee workers and employers who depend on the board to create stability in the workplace.

167.title: Alexander: States are Leading in Higher Education Innovation, Washington Getting in the Way
167.description: U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate education committee, today said the Washington bureaucracy, regulations and mandates are getting in the way of innovation in higher education in the states, which run the public 2- or 4-year institutions that three quarters of American students attend.

168.title: Alexander on Bill to Reverse Hobby Lobby Decision
168.description: U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) said today that the Senate Democrats' bill to roll back the Religious Freedom Restoration Act would "carve a giant hole out of America's religious freedom."

169.title: Alexander Opposes "Wasting a Week on a Political Stunt While Veterans are Standing in Line"
169.description:
U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, today voted against moving to the Senate Democrats' "political stunt" on student loans, saying the Senate shouldn't "waste time on it when veterans are standing in line waiting for us to take up a bipartisan proposal."

"This 'no' vote means 'no' to a week-long political stunt, 'no' to debt and taxes, 'yes' to moving today to a bipartisan solution to the problem of veterans standing in line at clinics. 'Yes' to appropriation bills after that that deal with cancer research and national defense and the other urgent needs of our country, also in a bipartisan way. 'Yes' to the way the Senate ought to run," Alexander said. "And 'no' to the practice of pulling a bill out of your pocket, putting it on the floor and wasting a week with a political stunt while veterans are standing in line at a clinic waiting for us to act."

Alexander added: "This is not a serious proposal. It's not going to help people. College graduates don't need a $1 a day subsidy to pay off their $27,000 loan, which is the average for a four-year degree. They need a job."

170.title: Alexander: Senate Dems' Student Loan Proposal Raises Taxes, Increases Debt to Offer $1-a-Day Subsidy
170.description:
Today in a speech on the Senate floor, U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, said that the Senate Democrats' student loan proposal "raises income taxes by $72 billion and could add up to $420 billion in new federal debt to offer a $1-a-day subsidy for some old student loans." 
 
"The Senate Democrats' proposal is a partisan, political stunt," Alexander said. "The Senate should send this proposal to the Senate education committee which is in the midst of a bipartisan reauthorization of the higher education act, the kind of serious discussion that produced last year's law that cut nearly in half interest rates for all NEW undergraduate student loans."

171.title: Alexander to Burwell: Republicans Are Ready to Repair Damage Obamacare Has Done
171.description:
Today in a speech on the Senate floor before the vote on the president's nominee for U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services, Sylvia Mathews Burwell, U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, laid out Republicans' step-by-step health care proposals that would "provide more freedom, more choices, and lower costs."

Alexander said of the health care system: "We'd like to turn it around and head it off in a different direction. Not back, but a different direction. We want to repair the damage that Obamacare has done. We want to prevent future damage as responsibly and rapidly as we can. We'd like to move in a different direction to put in place health care proposals that would increase freedom, increase choices, and lower costs. We trust Americans to make those decisions, to make them ourselves. We believe that is the American way."

172.title: FOX NEWS: Alexander: We Want to Provide "More Freedom, More Choices, Lower Costs" For Health Care
172.description:
Today on Fox News's "America's Newsroom," reporter Mike Emanuel highlighted the comments of U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), Ranking Member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, at a hearing on the president's nominee, Sylvia Burwell, for U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services, where Alexander laid out Republicans' step-by-step proposals to reduce health care costs and increase freedom and choice for Americans.

Sen. Alexander said to Burwell: "We want to move in a different direction to put in place proposals that provide more freedom, more choices and lower costs. We trust Americans to make those decisions for ourselves. We believe that is the American way. Since Obama will still be in office for the next two years. If you are confirmed, we will need your help to do that."

174.title: Alexander to Burwell: Here's What Republicans Would Do About Health Care if We Were in Charge
174.description:
At a hearing today on the president's nominee for U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services, U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate health committee, laid out Republicans' step-by-step proposals to reduce health care costs and increase freedom and choice for Americans.

"Here's what Republicans would do about health care if we were in charge: Republicans want to repair the damage Obamacare has done and prevent future damage. As responsibly and rapidly as we can, we want to move in a different direction to put in place proposals that provide more freedom, more choices and lower costs. We trust Americans to make these decisions for ourselves. That is the American Way."

He outlined specific proposals from Republican senators to provide Americans with "more choices to buy a plan that fits your health care needs and your budget, and more ability to choose the doctor you want."

175.title: Alexander: Secretary Sebelius's Absence Is "More Than Playing Hooky"
175.description:
U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) said today that the absence of Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius at a hearing to answer questions about a budget that she "helped write" was "more, I'm afraid, than the secretary playing hooky."
 
"This is getting to be a persistent problem with this administration regarding Article I of the Constitution and the Congress, the representatives of the people, as an inconvenience," Alexander said. "I think presidents ought to begin their terms by taking the cabinet down to Mount Vernon and reminding themselves that, while the chief executive is extremely important, the Founders didn't want a king. George Washington, who could have stayed as long as he lived as president, imprinted his humility and respect for the people in the Constitution that he helped to write"
 
"This is not right for a secretary of a department to not appear to defend the president's budget," said Alexander, the senior Republican on the health committee. "Where is the secretary of health and human services? She's still on the job. If the secretary of defense were still on the job and waiting on the next secretary to be confirmed, and we were invaded or Ukraine happened, would the secretary of defense not show up?"

176.title: Alexander: Dems Proposal to Hike Minimum Wage Will Destroy 500,000 Jobs; "There Are Better Ideas"
176.description:
Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, today on the Senate floor highlighted how the Democratic proposal to raise the minimum wage would eliminate 500,000 jobs and provide 80 percent of the benefits to American families above the poverty level, saying that "there are better ideas."
 
On the floor, Alexander said: "The issue is jobs... The American people want it to be easier to find a good paying job and the Democratic proposal that we're going to vote on this week as the solution to the jobs problem is a proposal that will eliminate 500,000 jobs. We're talking about jobs...  and the Democratic proposal to make it easier to find a job is to eliminate 500,000 jobs."
 
He added: "This is a constant parade of ideas that increase the big, wet smothering blanket of rules and regulations over the free enterprise system and that do nothing to make it easier to create jobs and easier to find a job. There are better ideas. Reform refundable tax credits benefit all low-income workers. Replace long-term unemployment compensation with job training. Change Obamacare's workweek definition from 30 hours to 40 hours to encourage full-time jobs. Use existing federal education dollars to give children of low-income families a $2,100 scholarship to choose a better school. All those would create more jobs and which those who want them could find a job more easily. That's what we should be about instead of pretending that we can pass a law in America and give many people a higher income. We can do that but when we do it, make no mistake about it, we're destroying 500,000 jobs and giving benefits to people above the poverty line instead of below."
 
The U.S. Senate will consider a vote on the Democratic minimum wage proposal this week.

177.title: Alexander, Burr: Unionization is No Solution for College Athletes

178.title: Alexander Amendment Would Give "More Flexibility for Working Parents"
178.description:
Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, today introduced a proposal to provide more workplace flexibility for working parents. Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid objected when Alexander and other Republican senators attempted to offer their proposals as amendments.

Alexander said: "This amendment is about giving working parents more flexibility so they can go to soccer games and piano recitals. It makes it clear that if you run a dry cleaner with three people in it, you don't have to go hire a lawyer to define a job for an employee with a child in such a way that the employee can go to the piano recital or soccer game. Instead of being about more litigation, it is about giving more flexibility for working parents."

He added: "Our fear is that this proposal, which is called 'Paycheck Fairness,' would actually limit the flexibility of employers to give to working parents more flexibility to go to their children's activities."

179.title: Alexander: Workers Need More Flexibility, Not Democrats' War on Jobs
179.description:
At a hearing of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee hearing today, Senator Alexander said workers today need more flexibility in the workplace, and said the Democrats' Paycheck Fairness Act would remove flexibility from the job market. 

He said the bill was part of a Democratic "war on jobs," waged with legislation such as minimum wage and Obamacare, which would make it more expensive to create jobs and harder to find work.

180.title: Alexander: Child Care Program Encourages Work and Job Training, Tells Story of Memphis Mother
180.description:
Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee today spoke on the Senate floor at the start of debate on a bill he coauthored to reauthorize the Child Care and Development Block Grant Program, which helps more than 1.5 million low-income children nationwide receive child care.

Alexander told the success story of one Memphis mother who benefited from the program: "I'm thinking of a young mother in Memphis, Tennessee, who was attending LeMoyne-Owen College earning a business degree. She had an infant child, so she put that child in a childcare center that she chose. The voucher through this program that we're talking about today provided about $500 to $600 a month to help for that. 

"Infant childcare is especially expensive, as, if you think about it, you can understand. The success part of the story is that she earned her degree. She's now an assistant manager at Wal-Mart in Memphis. The child who was the infant in the childcare center is 5 years old and she earns enough money to pay all the bill for [a second] child to go to the same childcare center while the money that helped her before is now available to some other mother." 

Alexander continued: "So this program encourages work, it encourages job training, and for those Americans who are low income and working or low income and training or educating themselves for a job, this helps them get that job. So this is an important bill for many, many families."

182.title: Alexander: Raising the Minimum Wage to Address Poverty is  "Stale, Bankrupt, Ineffective Policy"
182.description:
At a committee hearing today, U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the Ranking Member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee said:

"I believe families shouldn't live in poverty and I think the idea of raising the minimum wage to address that is a stale, bankrupt, ineffective policy. According to the Congressional Budget Office, [it] costs low-wage workers 500,000 jobs, makes it harder to create more jobs, and gives 80% of the benefits to families above the poverty level and we have a number of amendments and proposals that we are looking forward to offering to this bill when we have a markup that will create a pro-growth economy with more good jobs."

183.title: FOX NEWS: Alexander: Obama NLRB Continues to be More of a Union Advocate Than an Umpire
183.description:
Today on Fox News's "Happening Now," correspondent Shannon Bream highlighted the comments of Sen. Alexander, the top Republican on the Senate labor committee, on the National Labor Relations Board's intentions to finalize its rule authorizing "ambush elections," which shortens the length of time in which a labor union certification is held to as little as 10 days.

Alexander said the new rules are "...one more example of how the Obama National Labor Relations Board continues to be more of a union advocate then an umpire ... This latest effort is a political power play on behalf of unions that makes an end run around employers and forces workers to make decisions without all of the facts."

184.title: Alexander: Surgeon General's Office Shouldn't be "Bully Pulpit" for Obamacare, Gun Control
184.description:
U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the lead Republican on the Senate health committee, today pressed President Obama's nominee for U.S. surgeon general, Dr. Vivek Murthy, on whether he would use the "bully pulpit" as "the nation's doctor" to advance his ideological goals in favor of Obamacare and gun control.

Of Murthy's advocacy for Obamacare, Alexander said, "Much of your work has been devoted to electing the current president and advocating the new health care law ... I'd be reluctant to put into the surgeon general's office someone who would use that as a bully pulpit to promote a law I think is an historic mistake."

The senator also noted that Murthy is an advocate of gun control, once saying on the social media website Twitter that he was "tired of politicians...[who are] scared of the NRA." Alexander said, "I would hope you know that Americans have a First Amendment right to advocate the Second Amendment or any other amendment, and the Second Amendment is not a special interest group -- it's part of our Constitution."

185.title: Alexander On Fox: 11 Million $2,100 Scholarships for Kids a Real Answer to Inequality
185.description:
On Fox News's "Special Report with Bret Baier," U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the top Republican on the Senate education committee, spoke on his Scholarships for Kids Act that would address income inequality by giving "parents more freedom to choose a better school for their child."
 
Alexander told Shannon Bream: "If you had to ask Americans one single thing that was likely to make the most opportunity in helping you move from the back of the line to the front, it would be a good education." 
 
Alexander unveiled his legislation on Tuesday: "Today I am introducing legislation that would allow $2,100 federal scholarships to follow 11 million low-income children to any public or private accredited school of their parents' choice. This is a real answer to inequality in America: giving more children more opportunity to attend a better school."

186.title: Alexander Proposes 11 Million $2,100 "Scholarships for Kids"
186.description:
Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, today on the Senate floor highlighted the introduction of his legislation that would allow states to create $2,100 scholarships out of existing federal education dollars to follow 11 million low-income children to any public or private school of their parents' choice.
 
Alexander unveiled the proposal earlier today during a speech at the American Enterprise Institute: "Today I am introducing legislation that would allow $2,100 federal scholarships to follow 11 million low-income children to any public or private accredited school of their parents' choice. This is a real answer to inequality in America: giving more children more opportunity to attend a better school."

187.title: Alexander: Obamacare Brings Unwelcome Christmas Present, Unhappy New Year for Many Tennesseans
187.description:
Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, today on the Senate floor highlighted how Obamacare has increased costs and reduced health care choices for Tennesseans, and warned of more widespread consequences in the New Year.

On the floor, Alexander said: "The fact that at least 82,000 Tennesseans will begin to lose their individual health insurance policies starting Jan. 1 is an unwelcome Christmas present. And it'll be an unhappy New Year for many more Tennesseans who get their insurance on the job when Obamacare's burdensome mandates on employers kick in."

188.title: Alexander Tells CNBC Squawk Box on Obamacare: First Thing To Do is Put President's Promise Into Law
188.description:
This morning on CNBC's "Squawk Box," U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the top Republican on the Senate health committee, said Congress should put into law the president's promise that if you like your plan, you can keep it, and move forward with step-by-step reforms to increase competition and choices and lower health care costs.

Alexander told hosts Andrew Sorkin and Becky Quick: "The first thing is to try to put the President's promise into law. And Senator Johnson of Wisconsin has a bill to do that permanently. The President wants to do it until after the next election, but at least with the 5 million cancellations that we've already had, we can try to make it possible for many of those to keep those policies so there'd be fewer Americans hurt."

He added: "We'd move in a different direction, step-by-step, instead of trying to change the whole thing all at once as Obamacare did and as Hillary-care tried to do. We would try to move toward more competition, more choices, cheaper policies—that would allow Americans to actually buy affordable health care insurance."

189.title: Alexander: Senate Passage of Compounding Bill Makes it Clear Who's On the Flagpole
189.description:
Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, today on the Senate floor, praised Senate passage of legislation to help ensure the safety of compounded drugs and to track all prescription drugs from the time they are manufactured to the moment they are picked up at the drugstore. 

The Drug Quality and Security Act reflects a bipartisan, bicameral effort to address these drug safety and security issues.  It is aimed at helping prevent a future public health crisis like the 2012 meningitis outbreak tied to the New England Compounding Center and securing the pharmaceutical supply chain. The bill has now cleared both houses of Congress and will go on to the President to be signed into law

Alexander said: "This is very important piece of legislation on which senators and House members have been working on for a year. I am glad that it passed and I'm sure the president will sign it."

190.title: Tells Story of Emilie, One of Thousands of Tennesseans Losing Health Plans Under Obamacare
190.description:
Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee today spoke on the Senate floor about Tennesseans losing their health care plans because of Obamacare:

"The Tennessean reported yesterday morning in its headline that the state's largest underwriter is notifying 66,000 clients their policies don't meet ACA coverage requirements. In other words, they are losing those policies."

Alexander continued: "I have a letter from a woman named Emilie in middle Tennessee who was one of 16,000 Tennesseans who is part of yet another plan called CoverTN... [she said], 'I beg of you to continue to fight for those like me, who would only asked to be allowed to have what we already enjoy - fair health insurance plans at a fair price.'"

191.title: Alexander: Senate One Step Closer to Passing Compounding Agreement to Help Prevent Future Tragedies
191.description:
Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate health committee, today praised the Senate's vote, 97 to 1, to move forward on consideration of the legislative agreement he reached with House and Senate health committee leaders to make injections of compounded sterile drugs safer. The House passed the bill on Sept. 28. 
 
Alexander said: "The Senate should consider and pass this legislation immediately so we can help prevent another meningitis outbreak like the one that has killed 16 Tennesseans and made so many others so sick. The FDA commissioner has warned us that it's a matter of when, not if, this will happen again if we don't clarify oversight of compounders. Tonight's vote is an important step toward doing just that."

192.title: Alexander on FOX: Large Number of Americans to Find Insurance Canceled and Website Won't Work
192.description:
Today on Fox News's "America's News HQ," Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the top Republican on the Senate health committee, said the Obamacare exchange problems and the law's canceled policies may "leave several million Americans without insurance." 

Alexander told host Alisyn Camerota, "You've got until December 15th to actually -  [to get] through this website, find a way to sign up to get insurance that disappears on January 1. In Tennessee, we have 16,000 Tennesseans under a program called CoverTN. It was outlawed by Obamacare and we have been getting letters from those folks who are finding on the exchanges, their prices go up 400 percent. They are in real trouble."

He added: "The bigger problem is the large number of Americans who are going to be terrified as they approach the end of the year and find that their insurance is canceled and the website doesn't work and they either can't get insurance, or they can't afford insurance because the higher premiums takes it out of reach."

193.title: Alexander to Administration: "Why Not Put the President's Promise Into Law?"
193.description:
Fox News's "Shepard Smith Reporting," reported on Sen. Alexander's questions to hearing witness Marilyn Tavenner, administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, at today's HELP hearing on the Obamacare rollout. 

Alexander said: "So why not put the president's words into law and simply say if you like the plan you have--and we aren't going to decide for you, you can decide it as an individual--if you like the plan you have, you can keep it without having to change a thing."

You can watch more of the hearing here: http://www.help.senate.gov/newsroom/press/release/?id=1ac3bd68-d568-4205-b8fb-ced386fee477&groups=Ranking

194.title: Senator Alexander Questions CMS Administrator Tavenner at Obamacare Hearing 2

195.title: Senator Alexander at Obamacare Committee Hearing With CMS Administrator Tavenner

196.title: Alexander at Obamacare Hearing: Broken Promises, Broken Website an "Unwelcome Christmas Present"
196.description:
The senior Republican on the Senate health committee, in a hearing today on the Obamacare rollout, held up an iPad showing that WhiteHouse.gov still makes the following promise: "If you like your plan you can keep it and you don't have to change a thing due to the health care law." Alexander called on the Obama administration to put the president's promise -- "if you like your plan, you can keep it" -- into law, pointing to the thousands of Tennesseans who have received notice that their policies are being canceled because of Obamacare. 

Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) said: "The new promise is, 'If you want health care, go find it—on a website that the Administration says won't be working properly until the end of November.' That is an unwelcome Christmas present—only two weeks to shop for and buy a new insurance policy by December 15 so that you're covered next year when Obamacare outlaws your policy."

197.title: Alexander On Fox News: Sec. Sebelius Should Explain to Tennesseans Why They Can't Keep Insurance
197.description:
On Fox News's "Your World with Neil Cavuto," U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the top Republican on the Senate health committee, spoke about his call for Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius to resign because of the disastrous rollout of Obamacare.
 
Alexander told host Neil Cavuto: "[Sec. Sebelius] is going to Memphis tomorrow and while she is there I hope she explains to thousands of Tennesseans who are receiving cancelation letters, why they are going to be out of insurance starting on January 1 because the website won't work."

198.title: Alexander Tells Fox Business: Obamacare Website "Not the Biggest Problem"
198.description:
Last night, on Fox Business's "The Willis Report," U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate health committee, spoke about the Obamacare exchanges and his call for Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius to resign.

Alexander told host Gerri Willis: "The important thing is that the website is not the biggest problem. The biggest problem is going to be the canceled policies of millions of Americans who will find that starting on January 1 the policies that the president said they could keep are being canceled because they are not legal under Obamacare. Businesses will be finding that the costs are so high they will drop all lot of their coverage and their employees are going into Medicaid, and businesses are also struggling because of the 30-hour workweek requirement. They will have to cut pay—in effect—by putting employees on 30-hour work weeks to avoid the Obamacare requirement."

Alexander said of his legislation requiring weekly reports on Obamacare exchanges: "We want to know how many people have tried through the exchange to buy Obamacare? How many succeeded? In what zip code do they live? What level of insurance did they buy? We need to know that.  We ought to know that every week. Before the Internet age, RCA knew how many records Elvis was selling every day. Ford knew how many cars it was selling every day. McDonald's could tell you how many hamburgers they were selling every day. Now, in the middle of the Internet age, the Obama administration should be able to tell us really every day how many people signing up. What are they buying?"

He added: "[Sec. Sebelius] should step down, and somebody else should take charge."

199.title: Fox News: Alexander, Senior Republican on Senate Health Cmte, Calls for Resignation of Sec. Sebelius
199.description:
Fox News's "Special Report with Bret Baier," this evening reported on Senator Lamar Alexander's (R-Tenn.) call for President Obama to ask Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius to resign.

The senior Republican on the Senate health committee said, in a speech on the Senate floor: "Expecting this secretary to be able to fix in a few weeks what she has not been able to fix during the last three and one half years is unrealistic. It is throwing good money after bad."

200.title: Alexander Calls for Unanimous Passage of Bill Requiring Weekly Reports on Obamacare Exchanges
200.description: U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate health committee today introduced a bill requiring the administration to provide weekly reports on the Obamacare exchanges and said he would ask Tuesday for unanimous passage of the bill: "Before the Internet, RCA knew how many records Elvis was selling every day. Before the Internet, Ford knew how many cars they were selling every day. Before the Internet, McDonald's could tell you how many hamburgers it had sold each day. Yet the Obama administration cannot tell us how many Americans have tried to sign up for Obamacare."

201.title: Alexander Tells Fox News: Unworkable Website for Obamacare Mandate "Unacceptable"
201.description:
U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate health committee, today told Fox News's "Happening Now" that he's going to introduce a bill next week when the Senate reconvenes to "force" the administration to provide answers about the Obamacare rollout. 

"What we have right now is millions of Americans who are being told they have to buy insurance...on a website that doesn't work, or be fined by the Internal Revenue Service. Now that's completely unacceptable," Alexander said. "We want to know what is happening on the exchanges. We hear that half of 1 percent are all that were successful in the first week. I'd like to know how many were successful. I'd like to know what level of insurance they bought, what their zip code is. That ought to be information in the Internet age that's available every single day. It's Congress's job to have oversight over this." 

Alexander said: "I've asked the administration for a lot of information and I get no answers at all. So, we're going to introduce a law next week when the Senate reconvenes, and we're going to force it."

He added: "This is the Internet age—even before the Internet age, McDonalds could tell you how many hamburgers it was selling every day. If the administration were rolling this out properly, it would report every day on how many people visited, how many were successful, what their zip codes were. So, they would be proud of their new health care law."

"All this secrecy," Alexander said, "this business of telling health insurers not to even let the people know how many people are signing up—that breeds a lack of confidence in what you're doing, it's not a winning strategy, it wouldn't work in the private sector.

"I would expect the Senate Democrats to help me join in oversight of this law and let's have some information about it," he said. " I would think that since Democrats passed the law that they'd like people to know how it's working. 

Alexander said of his legislation: "This isn't really complicated information. [I'd like to know] how many people tried to sign up? How many were successful? What zip code are they in? What level of insurance did they buy? Here in Tennessee, people are finding when they get on that their individual insurance might cost twice as much as it did before. Their family insurance might cost twice as much as it did before. That is important information."

Alexander also told Fox News: "Somebody needs to be on the flagpole for this and somebody needs to be fired. If the President isn't going to resign, he should fire somebody else."

202.title: Fox Business: Alexander to Introduce Bill Requiring Weekly Reports on Obamacare Exchanges
202.description:
Fox Business this morning reported on a bill to be introduced by U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) requiring "weekly reports on the Obamacare exchanges as political pressure continues and exchanges online are not working well."

You can find more on the bill here: http://www.help.senate.gov/newsroom/press/release/?id=e4f75951-2814-406b-87fb-0c3aafc37dbc&groups=Ranking

203.title: Fox News: Alexander, Issa Investigating Obamacare site's technical failures
203.description:
Fox News this morning reported on the letter sent by U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) and Chairman of the House Oversight Committee Darrell Issa (R-Calif.) to Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius calling for details on the Obamacare exchange web site's technical failures.

You can find more on the letter here: http://www.help.senate.gov/newsroom/press/release/?id=556468d9-57d0-46b1-a41f-05b26f7a25a7&groups=Ranking

204.title: Alexander: "We Can Change the Health Care Law and Keep the Government Going"
204.description: Sen. Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the senior Republican on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions committee, spoke on the Senate floor this afternoon about Obamacare, the opening of the exchanges tomorrow, and the next steps in funding the government. He said: "We need not be thinking about shutting down the government. We need to be thinking about a way to fund the government and change the health care law at the same time."

205.title: Alexander Calls for Accountability at Senate Hearing on Health-Care Associated Infections
205.description:
At a Senate hearing today on health-care associated infections, Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) asked Jonathan B. Perlin, President of Clinical and Physician Services and Chief Medical Officer for Nashville-based Hospital Corporation of America and a witness at the hearing:

"I have brought up in hearings in this committee the importance of accountability -- we are going through that with dealing with the tragedy of fungal meningitis and compounding pharmacies. 

Based on your experience, what can [Congress] do to fit into the strategy to reach [the goal of eliminating health-care acquired infections by 2020] without making it more difficult for hospitals and managers to reach that goal. How can we put somebody on the flagpole? How can we make it clear who is accountable for reaching that goal by 2020 so that we don't have infections in hospitals when we go to get well and instead get sick?"

206.title: Alexander: Today's American Higher Education System is Like the Auto Industry of the 1970s
206.description:
U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), the Ranking Member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee said at today's education hearing, the first in a series the committee is holding on reauthorization of the Higher Education Act, that the higher education system "is like the American automobile industry of the 1970s. First, it offers a remarkable number of choices of the best products in the world at a reasonable cost.  Second, it is not doing much about challenges that will require major adjustments if, 20 years from now, it wants to be able to make that same claim of superior choices at a reasonable cost."

"I have asked my staff to consider drafting a new Higher Education Act from scratch. Start all over. Include everything that needs to be included and consider new regulations that needed to be written," he added.

207.title: Fox News: Alexander on Obamacare Delay: "No Train Wreck Has Ever Had This Many Warning Signs"
207.description: Fox News's "Happening Now" this morning reported on the latest Obamacare delay, quoting U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), Ranking Member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, said, "I've been warning that a train wreck is coming with this law, but the truth is that no train wreck has ever had this many warning signs."

208.title: Senate Tells Any President: "You May Not Abuse Constitutional Right" of Recess Appts
208.description: Sen. Lamar Alexander (R. Tenn) said today, in a speech on the Senate floor: "The United States Senate is saying to not just this president but to any president, Republican or Democrat, that you may not abuse your constitutional right of recess appointments by making appointments when the Senate itself determines that it is not in recess. To do so is an affront to the separation of powers, and it undermines the checks and balances that were placed upon the executive at the beginning of our country as a way of preserving our liberties. That's an important step in the history of constitutional law in this country, and I'm glad to see that it has been done in this way."

209.title: Senator Alexander: Student Loan Bill Makes Loans "Cheaper, Simpler, More Certain"
209.description: Today in a speech on the Senate floor about the Bipartisan Student Loan Certainty Act, Sen. Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) said: "This permanent, market-based plan makes students' loans cheaper, simpler and more certain. It ends the annual game of Congress playing politics with student loan interest rates at the expense of students planning their futures."

210.title: Alexander on Senate Floor - Voting Against President's Labor Secretary Nominee
210.description:
Today on the Senate floor on voting against confirmation of President Obama's nominee for U.S. Secretary of Labor, Thomas Perez, Senator Alexander said he "supports any president's right to have an up-or-down vote on his cabinet nominees—never in our nation's history has the Senate used a filibuster to block a cabinet official from taking his or her seat." 

"Mr. Perez's involvement in a quid pro quo arrangement between the Department of Justice and the city of St. Paul seems to me an extraordinary amount of wheeling and dealing outside the normal responsibilities of the Assistant Attorney General over the Civil Rights Division," said Alexander.

211.title: Senator Alexander: Bipartisan Student Loan Bill "Saves Billions of Dollars for 11M Students"
211.description:
Today, U.S. Senators Alexander, Joe Manchin (D-WV), Richard Burr (R-NC), Angus King (I-ME), Tom Coburn (R-OK), Tom Carper (D-DE), Tom Harkin (D-IA), and Dick Durbin (D-IL) introduced a bipartisan compromise, the Bipartisan Student Loan Certainty Act, to lower interest rates for 100% of borrowers who have taken out, or will take out, a new federal student loan after July 1, 2013.

"This long-term, market-based solution means that interest rates on all undergraduate loans—which are two-thirds of all student loans—will be 3.86 percent this year," said Senator Alexander.  "Rates on all other student loans will also be reduced. This saves billions of dollars for the 11 million students who will borrow money to go to college this year."

212.title: Alexander on Senate Floor Speaks Before Student Loan Vote
212.description: Today in a speech on the Senate floor before the vote on a student loan proposal supported by some Democrats, Sen. Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) said: "Eighty percent of students who have subsidized loans, the low-income students, also have the unsubsidized loans. When you only take care of these subsidized loans, you're leaving 7 million students with unsubsidized loans up here high and dry and nobody's taking care of them. You're hurting both the middle-income families and the low-income families when you have an incomplete solution."

213.title: Alexander: Democratic Student Loan Bill "Leaves Over 7M Middle-Income Students Twisting in the Wind"
213.description:
The senior Republican on the U.S. Senate education committee today in a speech on the Senate floor called on Senate Democrats to support a proposal to lower student loan rates for all student borrowers, rather than the Democratic proposal scheduled for a vote tomorrow that will lower rates only on subsidized Stafford loans for a year.

Sen. Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) said: "The only proposal that we're going to be voting on tomorrow appears to be one that will leave over 7 million middle-income college students twisting in the wind paying about twice as much in interest rates as they should be paying."

214.title: Alexander: "What is Good About a Short-Term Political Fix that Makes Students Pay More?"
214.description: Today in a speech on the Senate floor on student loans, in response to remarks by Sen. Patty Murray (D-Wash.) Sen. Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) said: "What is good about a short-term political fix that makes middle-income students and graduate students pay more—hundreds of millions of dollars more over the next ten years? What's good about that? All it does is provide an opportunity to make a well-rehearsed political speech about student loans. We all want to encourage students to go to college. We're looking for a way to give them some predictability and some certainty so that a student doesn't have to worry when they graduate from high school in Tennessee, where I went, that Congress isn't going to get its job done and all they're going to do is stand up and make political speeches that have nothing to do with the issue."

215.title: Alexander Offers Plan to Restore "Freedom and Choice to States, Teachers, and Parents"
215.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) offered a proposal to fix No Child Left Behind, saying, "what we're trying to do is free the states to help children in 100,000 schools meet their needs in individual ways...the real difference is whether we think the responsibility is here in Washington or at home—we believe it's at home."

Alexander, Ranking Member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, offered the proposal as an alternative at a committee markup today of a Democratic proposal to reauthorize the law.

Alexander said: "This is not a proposal just for Republicans.  We believe this proposal represents the views and will attract the support of the governors leading the charge for education reform, teachers who value the freedom to teach, parents who want more choices for their children, and state legislators who are working for better schools."

216.title: Alexander Speaks Before Senate Vote on Student Loan Bill
216.description:
Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), speaking this morning before the Senate vote on the Republican student loan bill which would set all student loan rates to a single market-based rate, said "we don't have a real disagreement—the House of Representatives has passed a bill based on the same idea, the President of the United States, President Obama, has presented a budget to the Senate a few weeks ago based on the same idea."

Alexander said: "Our bill takes advantage of today's low rates and lowers rates on all new student loans this year to below 5 percent—it's fair to students, it's fair to taxpayers, it's a permanent solution and it's the same idea that the House has already passed and the same idea that the president has recommended. I wish all of our serious issues opened with proposals from the president and the House of Representatives and Senate Republicans that were as close together as they are on this issue. We should sit down together and spend the next three weeks saying: 'We all have the same idea, we have a serious issue here, it affects millions of students - 66 percent of students graduating from high school—so let's work together and show the country we can do this.'"

Alexander, with Senators Tom Coburn (R-Okla.) Richard Burr (R-N.C.), and Johnny Isakson (R-G.A.), in April introduced the "Comprehensive Student Loan Protection Act," a bill that requires that, for each academic year, all newly-issued Stafford, Graduate PLUS, and Parent PLUS loans be set to the U.S. Treasury 10-year borrowing rate plus 3 percentage points. It would lower the interest rate for this coming school year for all newly issued federal student loans to a fixed rate of 4.75 percent, based on the May 15 auction rate of 1.75 percent.

217.title: Alexander: "Republicans Have a Plan to Make Student Loans Simpler and Smarter for the Student"
217.description:
At a Senate press conference today on student loan reform, U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), Ranking Member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee said,

"Republicans have a plan to make those student loans simpler and smarter for the student, so we can encourage them to go on to college. It's very simple—the same rate for all of the loans. All new loans for next year would be at a rate of less than 5 percent. Students could count on that. And if they consolidate their loans there would be a cap on that at the end."

Alexander added: "There is no reason why we can't work together with the president and the House of Representatives to come up with a permanent solution to student loans that reduces rates for 100% of the loans - the new loans, and do it by July 1."

218.title: Alexander on Fox News: Obama Administration "Really Thumbing Its Nose at Congress"
218.description:
On Fox News's "Fox & Friends" this morning, U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), Ranking Member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, told host Steve Doocy, "Our founders didn't want a king, so they created Congress and they created limits on the executive, and this president--whether making recess appointments when we're not in recess or trying to avoid advice and consent in that way, or trying to avoid the appropriations process by appointing czars, or creating, in effect, a national school board by using the waiver authority--they've been pushing,  really thumbing their nose at Congress."

On reports of HHS Secretary Sebelius fundraising for a private entity to implement the health care law, Alexander said: "We have a Constitution that says only the Congress can spend money and we have federal laws that say if Congress says no, you can't make an end run."

Alexander added: "This be would be the same thing as if the president asked Congress--said, 'I need nine jet planes,' and Congress said, 'We'll give you eight,' and the president went to his friends, raised a couple million dollars and bought a ninth one."

219.title: Alexander on CNBC's Kudlow Report: "Is HHS Secretary Sebelius Making an End Run Around Congress?"
219.description:
U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), Ranking Member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, spoke with Larry Kudlow on CNBC about his call, with Senators Hatch and Coburn, for the Health and Human Services Department Inspector General to investigate whether Secretary Sebelius is "raising money from people she regulates, and more importantly, is she making an end run around Congress by doing with private money and a private entity what Congress refused to do?"

"If Congress says you can't do it, the Obama administration can't go out and raise private money and set up a private entity to do it anyway."

220.title: Alexander on Fox Business: We're Trying to Find Out "Is HHS Secretary Doing an End-Run on Congress?"
220.description:
U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), Ranking Member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, today spoke with Fox Business about his call, with Senators Hatch and Coburn, for the Health and Human Services Department Inspector General to investigate whether Secretary Sebelius is "raising money outside of the government to do what Congress has refused to do--that's illegal, the constitution doesn't permit it."

"Many administrations have chafed at the limits that a Congress, with the exclusive power to appropriate money, puts on an executive. But the Obama adminstration has been more flagrant than most."

221.title: Alexander:Sebelius's coordinating w/ private entities on Obamacare part of administration 'pattern'
221.description:
On FOX News' "On the Record" with Greta Van Susteren, Senator Alexander said that HHS Secretary Sebelius's fundraising and coordinating with private entities to implement the president's healthcare law is "a pattern we've been seeing. Just like the president making recess appointments when the Senate isn't in recess. The Founders didn't want a king. They created a Congress and a Bill of Rights to stop the king, and these end runs around Congress are specifically illegal."

Alexander continued, "This sounds like the way Iran Contra started. Benghazi sounds like the way Watergate started. The excessive looking for leaks among up to 100 A.P. employees sounds like the way the White House plumbers started. The IRS sounds like the "enemies list" back in the Nixon administration. All of these are very unpleasant echoes, and an administration ought to not want that to happen."

222.title: Alexander Asks Secretary Sebelius For Details on Fundraising
222.description: In a floor speech today, Senator Lamar Alexander said he would  call on the Government Accountability Office to investigate Secretary Sebelius's fundraising and coordinating with private entities to implement health care law.

223.title: Alexander: Compounding draft legislation "sets a clear line for who's in charge"
223.description:
At a hearing today of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee on proposed drug compounding legislation, Ranking Member U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) told an official of the Food and Drug Administration that any efforts to mix oversight responsibilities for compounding manufacturers or pharmacies would "just leave us where we are."

Alexander said: "It's important for a facility to know that if it makes a sterile product, in advance of a prescription, and sells it across the state line, the facility has one regulator and that is the FDA, period. The doctor knows that, the customer knows that, the patient knows that, and the FDA knows that, and everybody knows that it is the FDA's job to make sure that place is safe."

The draft legislation, Alexander said, "tries to set clear lines for who's in charge and when they're in charge."

224.title: Alexander: "When You Walk Into a Pharmacy or Facility, It Will Be Clear Who is in Charge"
224.description:
At a hearing today of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee on proposed drug compounding legislation, Ranking Member U.S. Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) told an official of the Food and Drug Administration that any efforts to mix oversight responsibilities for compounding manufacturers or pharmacies would "just leave us where we are."

Alexander said: "It's important for a facility to know that if it makes a sterile product, in advance of a prescription, and sells it across the state line, the facility has one regulator and that is the FDA, period. The doctor knows that, the customer knows that, the patient knows that, and the FDA knows that, and everybody knows that it is the FDA's job to make sure that place is safe."

The draft legislation, Alexander said, "tries to set clear lines for who's in charge and when they're in charge."

225.title: Alexander Speaks Before Senate Vote on School Choice Amendment
225.description:
Senator Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), speaking this evening before the Senate voted on the school choice amendment he introduced with Senator Rand Paul (R-Ky.), said the legislation was "designed to help 11 million low-income children in this country."

Alexander said: "We appropriate $14.5 billion every year through our Title I federal funding. It's supposed to go to [low-income students] but it doesn't get there. That's agreed upon by both the left and the right. For example, Marguerite Roza writing for the Center for American Progress says that the difference between school expenditures is often substantial and she pointed out that the money goes to schools where teachers are paid more but the children aren't necessarily the poor children. And so the poorer children, the ones we intend to help, are left in schools with less money. Sometimes the money can add up to quite a bit. The same analysis is then found by the Fordham Foundation, I would say that's a center-right organization.

"So, we're suggesting to let the money follow the child to the school, whether it's public or private."

The amendment, which was cosponsored by Senators Pat Toomey (R-Penn.), Marco Rubio (R-Fla.), and Mitch McConnell (R-Ky.), was not agreed to, by a vote of 39 to 60.

226.title: Alexander-Paul Amdmt Lets Title I Dollars Follow Low-Income Students to Schools They Attend
226.description:
Washington, D.C., March 21 -- U.S. Senators Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.) and Rand Paul (R-Ky.) today introduced a school choice amendment that would allow $14.5 billion in existing federal Title I education dollars to follow 11 million low-income children to any accredited school, public or private.

The senators said, "Under current law too often these education dollars don't reach the low-income children they're supposed to help. The simplest way to fix this is to allow the $1,300 per child in existing federal funding to follow children to the school they attend."  Alexander and Paul are members of the senate's Health, Education Labor Committee and Alexander is the ranking Republican member.
